in a customized D&D game. Furthermore, we highlight the importance of the AI's
ability to guide the game's progression, and how this can be quantified and
addressed, providing a roadmap for future research into AI cooperation and
communication within the same environment. The findings are available on GitHub
at https://github.com/ericchenchamber/DandDAlignmentProject, and the paper is
published on ArXiv at https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.03798.

Physics and chemistry principles combine to explain the complex structures of proteins, particularly those with intricate configurations like knots. Environmental factors and chemical compositions of proteins significantly influence their configurations, but modeling the formation of knots in proteins remains computationally demanding when protosequences are considered. A novel approach is introduced using topological methods to identify stable pathways for bent proteins within various degrees of curvature. This "selection by topology" strategy identifies optimal pathways for proteins subjected to gradual bending based on their inherent complexity. The method is applied to identify stable bending pathways for randomly created knots and the well-known Adkins-Statton-Edwards model, as well as the Amys-Edwards-Imaizumi-Whittington (AEIW) model. In addition, this "selection by topology" approach is utilized to identify stable bending pathways for real proteins with intricate knots, including the Pdb code 1k89 with its 10-fold interlocking structure and the Pdb code 3o14 with its 5-fold interlocking structure.

We establish mapping category groups for the symplectic immappings from all blowups of standard tori in a four-dimensional symplectic manifold, denated as $\blowup_{\mathbb{R}^2_+}T^2$ and $\blowup_{\mathbb{R}^2_-}T^2$, with respect to the relevant admissibility conditions, within the entire range of their symplectic capacities.

A new, irregular version of the Nambu-Goldstone (NG) theorem is presented and applied to both relativistic and nonrelativistic quantum field theories. According to this version of the NG theorem, a spontaneously broken continuous global symmetry results in the creation of a nontrivial, positive-definite, pole in the corresponding vacuum expectation value (VV) of a local, scalar operator, found within the Fourier transform of such an expectation value as opposed to a particle. In scenarios where the spontaneous symmetry breaking leads to no particle, a "type-B" or "irregular" NG theorem applies, which guarantees a pole in the two-point correlation function of the order parameter, potentially representing a new physical phenomenon. This theory is shown to explain various instances of spontaneous symmetry breaking in both the Standard Model and extensions, including the Higgs mechanism, technicolor models, and superconductivity.

Current language models effectively generate text but fail to accurately capture non-sequence data like tables and graphs, which is essential for representing counterfactual statements. To address this limitation, we develop an automated framework for extracting phrasal counterfactuals from text, based on table data. This framework relies on an expanded prompt for language models that manually selects counterfactual statements. We manually create prompt components that highlight the contrastive nature of counterfactual statements, and we discover that these components guide the models to generate accurate counterfactual statements. Furthermore, we identify certain structures within tables that facilitate the generation of counterfactual statements. Our research demonstrates that this method produces high-quality counterfactual statements that are comparable to existing approaches, and it empowers a model to learn from tabular data and infer meaningfully from statements such as "although the salary of a teacher is $50k annually, the salary of a CEO can be $500k annually."

Epitaxial growth on distant surfaces occurs when vapor phase atoms or
  molecules reach a substrate via the atmosphere, with a governing balance
  between interactions including the van der Waals at the interface, as well
  as an infinite pinhole at the interface that acts as a source of
  condensation equilibrium.  Precursors such as sputtered Sn can deviate from
  this balance and require a more comprehensive model that includes dynamics
  akin to vacuum deposition.  We present a unifying approach to both distant
  and van der Waals epitaxy that identifies the regimes where each form is
  applicable and identifies strategies to promote each form of equilibrium.  We
  find that a surface flux that is too high can promote van der Waals epitaxy,
  whereas a flux that is low enough promotes distant epitaxy.  These findings
  are supported by experimentation in preparation for publication.

Recently, a new type of code known as $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear codes has been introduced, resulting in a reduction of the reduction of the set of prime numbers where codes can be optimally encoded. This paper investigates $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}}$-linear codes, focusing on their properties and characteristics, specifically their rank, $\mathcal{d}_\text{B}$, $\mathcal{d}_\mathbb{Z}$, and $\mathcal{d}_\mathbb{R}$, as well as their duals, the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-linear codes, whose parameters are given by $[2p^2n_1,p,n_\mathbb{Z}+1,\min(p-1,n_\mathbb{Z})]$, and their dual, the $\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear codes whose parameters are given by $[p^2n_1 + pn_2,d_\mathbb{B},\max (p^n-1,p^n-1),\min (p^n-1,p^n-1)]$. Ultimately, the concept of the "null space" of $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}}$-linear codes is introduced and some of their characteristics are investigated.

In the context of semi-supervised learning, the goal is to maximize the utilization of readily available positive labels while minimizing the reliance on potentially inaccurate negative labels. A current challenge arises when attempting to differentiate between positive and negative labels, as each positive label can correspond to multiple instances, some of which are actually negative. This paper presents a novel approach that treats each positive label as an independent, single-label classification problem, utilizing a separate network to solve these issues. This module then generates multi-label instances, which are categorized into positive and high-density negative instances. Both networks process the positive label instances and the negative instances in a unified feature space, allowing for more effective utilization of the positive labels and more stringent definition of the negative label space. The proposed method eliminates the necessity of manually defining the negative label space and significantly enhances the performance of multi-label classification when only the positive label space is available.

This study establishes a 2-categorical adjunction linking the 2-functor of complex
conformal field theory (CCFT) constructions to a 2-monad on 2-Cob, a category
representing oriented closed surfaces and their cobordisms. This adjunction enables
the translation of conformal data into a framework capable of generating novel
theories through iteration, potentially yielding innovations beyond the original
conformal field theory in two-dimensional topological field theories. It is further
shown that this general result implies a specific adjunction involving complexified
Voronoi's 2-functor, following a proof of the equivalence between the 2-free
completion of a surface category and its semi-classical reduction.

The nature of high-energy gamma-rays produced in radio galaxies at short distances is still unclear. It's proposed that magnetic fields generated by magnetohydrodynamic processes in radio galaxy acceleration disks can trap high-speed particles, which in turn contribute to the gamma-rays observed through both the annihilation of positrons and the de-excitation of nuclear particles. Based on this theory, we created a model to quantify the intensity of these gamma-rays, and it is found that even the highest-energy outputs from local supermassive black holes can be accounted for by these magnetic fields. This is particularly evident in galaxies like M87, where the model aligns well with observed data, and it is proposed that this theory may also hold true for other galaxies, such as Centaurus A.

The goal of heart sound signal categorization is to accurately identify normal or abnormal cardiac conditions.
Despite the importance of this task, accurate heart sound diagnosis is challenging due to various factors,
including heart diseases and external interference noises that can distort heart sounds.
To effectively identify normal and abnormal conditions, this paper addresses two key issues:
first, it solves the problem of identifying hearts sounds recorded with added interference,
using noise reduction techniques that learn from the data.
Second, it tackles the issue of assessing
heart sounds recorded at different probe positions, which occur with different frequencies and time deformations.
Our proposed approach combines different aposteriori filtering methods for interference reduction
and employs a deep neural network to classify different heart sound signals.
The effectiveness of the proposed solution is demonstrated through extensive experiments
on heart sound signal datasets recorded without noise and with various noise signals,
achieving high classification accuracy.

The rapid expansion of information technology and wearable health devices creates significant potential for distributed medical knowledge. Nevertheless, several challenges hinder this process, primarily related to security and privacy concerns. In response to these obstacles, FedHealth, a federated transfer learning framework for wearable healthcare, is proposed. It aims to achieve a secure and privacy-preserving transfer of knowledge across wearable devices in the healthcare domain. FedHealth comprises two main phases, transfer knowledge and local fine-tuning. In the first phase, it is divided into three sub-phases, knowledge transfer among peers with similar demographics, transfer of knowledge among different demographics with a graph neural network, and knowledge transfer between mobile devices and healthcare settings. It has been design that employs robust and efficient encryption techniques, such as homomorphic encryption and shamir's secret reconstruction, to ensure the safety of shared information. In the second phase, it is intended for a particular user to fine-tune the model locally with their own data. The experimental results show that FedHealth, a innovative and practical framework, offers enhanced accuracy, generalization ability, and data security for wearable healthcare applications, as evidenced by comparable performance metrics to those achieved through traditional methods, while also demonstrating resistance to various attacks, including vertical and horizontal data breaches.

This paper examines three portfolio improvement methods that provide a higher level of protection against significant losses. In the context of risk management, we analyze and distinguish various approaches, specifically comparing the Hedge Portfolio with the Portfolio Assistant and a Recourse Hedge, each employing different optimization frameworks. By establishing clear differences, the contrast between these methods becomes more apparent when considering the trade-off between risk and return.

This document consists of the original title and a compiled list of references for a research paper on automated software management. The primary focus is on presenting a method to automatically integrate, build, and install software dependencies in accordance with the requirements specified in a project. This is achieved by leveraging Construct, another set of data-driven pipelines. The document also includes relevant background information and demonstrates the practical application of the techniques discussed.

This study investigates the impact of a specific operation known as the swap principle in a particular type of control problem involving a cost function that exhibits right-continuous and non-left-continuous behavior over time. The time axis in this context is defined by the classical right sides of its intervals. The analysis in the paper contrasts two approaches to a simple scenario where the cost is either incurred at the start or the end of each interval, demonstrating that the non-equivalence of these approaches results in a non-intuitive outcome. The paper also delves into various methods to resolve this issue, as well as extends the analysis to more intricate situations where the cost function includes more information. The theoretical findings are applied to a simple economic model of supply and supply accumulation.

In a new effective field theory describing a U(1) gauge group at a low energy level, two types of scalar leptoquarks, denoted as $S_1$ and $S_2$, are integrated. The constraints of lepton and baryon number conservation are applied to this model. By incorporating the appropriate counterterms within the theory, the one-loop radiative corrections to the production of these leptoquarks in proton-proton collisions are calculated. The characteristics of the resulting trilinear and bilinear coupling constants are detailed, along with the optimal conditions for detecting this model, particularly when it decays into quarks, at the Large Hadron Collider.

Observations indicating that polycyclic aromatic compounds in the interstellar medium are partially deionized support the suggestion that neutral atomic carbon lines can provide a precise measurement of molecular gas in galaxies. It is proposed that a significant proportion of neutral atomic carbon lines in dense molecular gas are deionized through non-thermal mechanisms, which this paper examines in depth. By utilizing a variety of radiative transfer and chemical modeling tools, we aim to provide an in-depth explanation for non-equilibrium chemistry and the deionization of neutral atomic carbon lines in dense molecular gas reservoirs. The analysis reveals that electron impact processes contribute substantially to deionizing neutral atomic carbon lines through interactions with molecular hydrogen, cyanide, and other molecules in certain temperature ranges. The implications of this phenomenon are explored with regard to the interpretation of far-infrared carbon monoexides lines, the development of new utility for the deionization rate as an observational parameter that could guide the selection of follow-up observations, and the use of neutral atomic carbon lines as indicators of molecular gas temperatures.

Let's imagine a hamman box containing n balls, n/2 of which are painted red and the rest blue. Shuffling the box generates a permutation, and we can see the sequence of red and blue colors. Given such a sequence of red and blue colors, our aim is to reconstruct the underlying permutation. If we measure the discrepancy between the original and reconstructed permutations using the Hamming distance, a challenging problem arises. Especially so for permutations differing by more than a tiny fraction of n positions. In this research, a reconstruction algorithm is proposed that effectively tackles this difficulty. Even in the worst-case scenarios, if we sort the N permutations by their difference, the median relative error grows very slowly, exhibiting nearly polynomial behavior.

We conducted simulations to generate pulsar timing array signals from merging eccentric binaries to evaluate the efficiency of a GAUSSIAN process code in handling highly complex, relativistic events. Our analysis focused on pulsar signals from binary black holes and neutron star binaries with varying levels of eccentricity, semi-major axes, and masses. Our results demonstrate that while the code is capable of efficiently generating semi-precise pulsar timing data, the computations for less eccentric events, we found the code to be a precise and efficient tool for generating pulsar timing data in preparation for future observations.

We establish a "velocity procedure" for ASEP that leads to its TASEP-convergence, extending a previous approach developed by Pr\'el`eve and Vir`ag. This method entails showing two key properties: first, a symmetry in the system's dynamics where faster particles' contributions cancel out, and second, a form of stochastic ordering in the system. Utilizing this procedure, we derive multiple TASEP limits for ASEP, and in doing so, we show that certain data permutations in the step-initially filled TASEP limit interlaced particle process converge to those in the two-type ASEP. These limitations were previously conjectured and established by other researchers.

Since the beginning of the global COVID-19 outbreak caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, an extensive range of epidemiological models have been developed and examined. This examination will begin by tracing the history and evolution of epidemic modelling, before delving into a detailed exploration of key features of the SARS-CoV-2 outbreak and their associated mathematical implications. Subsequent sections will compare and contrast basic epidemic models in response to various outbreak characteristics, including super-spreading events, asymptomatic infection, and re-infection. Furthermore, an overview of recent research and discussions will be presented, highlighting the biophysical principles that underpin these models, and their potential utility for guiding public health policy.

We demonstrate that a spin-polarized spinor gas can undergo a three-body recombination process, effectively turning particles into molecules through a unique mechanism. By studying the dynamics of a one-dimensional atomic Bose-Einstein condensate with permanent dipole moments subjected to a weak two-body repulsive interaction, we observe that at optimal conditions, nearly all atoms participate in irreversible three-body collisions, resulting in the formation of stable molecules via a 1D recombination process that conserves momentum. Unlike typical processes, these molecules have an excitation energy equal to that of the atoms plus a photon, and they exhibit a specific helicity derived from the initial spin configuration. We further explain that this process allows for the direct generation of molecules with particular quantum properties, and it is applicable to a broad range of dipolar molecules that have multiple internal spin states.

A novel DNA data storage system called Hierarchy-Information Encoding (HIE) has been developed, which is designed to efficiently handle hierarchical DNA information and prevent hybridization errors during the retrieval process. In HIE, a new method called Clustered Huffman Encoding (CHE) has been developed to manage hierarchical information, while an optimized hybridization-assist sequence (HAS) encoding scheme is used to enhance the information capacity and reading success of DNA. Experimental results show that compared to traditional encoding methods, the HIE framework achieves a 52% - 75% reduction in hybridization errors and significantly enhances the accuracy of DNA data retrieval. Furthermore, the HIE framework allows for a flexible and effective way to organize and update information on DNA, which can lead to substantial cost savings in scenarios where hierarchical information needs to be adjusted or information must be deleted and replaced. Cost analyses have shown that by utilizing the HIE framework, a 52% - 69% reduction in additional synthesis costs can be achieved when updating hierarchical information, and even more significant savings can be achieved when deleting and substituting information.

The complex nature of non-linear partial differential equations like the shallow water equations poses challenges in understanding and modeling a wide range of phenomena including river flow, sediment transport and lake hydrodynamics. The primary objective of this research is to introduce a novel hybrid approach that combines the multilevel fast snapshot Galerkin method and neural network acceleration techniques to create a high-efficiency solver for these equations. The proposed method leverages supervised learning to significantly accelerate the application of the time-integration operator, enabling the shallow water equations to be resolved with a level of accuracy that surpasses traditional neural ODE solvers. Through extensive numerical experiments, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by achieving a level of precision while reducing computational costs.

HDR photography combines multiple photos captured at various exposure settings to broaden the dynamic range and prevent image overexposure or underexposure. This research presents a exposure selection method and a fusion method deep learning models for automatic high dynamic range creation on mobile devices. The proposed exposure choice deep learning model determines the optimal number of images to combine and the specific exposure settings for each, based on an scene's dynamic range. In addition, the proposed fusion model leverages an attention mechanism to capture inter-pixel relationships and enhance image details. The proposed framework's effectiveness is demonstrated through comprehensive testing.

Deep neural networks have significantly advanced in recent years due to their superior performance in various tasks. However, they often mimic complex patterns without truly understanding the underlying structure of the data, which may lead to poor generalization capabilities. In this report, we introduce the concept of "causal neural learning" and explore the potential for incorporating causal structures into neural networks to enhance their generalization performance. We provide a fundamental framework for this approach and discuss potential applications and open research questions in this emerging field.

This paper presents a new conjecture that fills the knowledge gap between low dimensions of 2 and higher dimensions of 4, offering an alternative to the well-established b-principle in its intermediate dimension3 case. We provide a few scenarios where our conjecture can be verified and outline its connection to existing theories. Furthermore, we discuss the name "b-principle" originates from its relationship to the fundamental theorem of calculus, highlighting its dependence on the differentiation and integration operators rather than the specific differentiation and integration principles they represent.

Understanding the mechanical behavior of the heart at a micro level is a comparative study focusing on mathematical models that simulate cardiac mechanics. These models, which incorporate complex, non-uniform tissue properties, are solved using advanced numerical methods and multilevel preconditioners designed for efficient computation across multiple processors. The study investigates scalable multilevel preconditioners, including a newly proposed variant, to determine their suitability for achieving large-scale simulations without loss in temporal resolution. The results show that their performance varies depending on the geometric shape of the heart, with some preconditioners demonstrating superior scalability in certain scenarios. The multilevel preconditioners performed more effectively than the traditional ILU preconditioner in most cases, providing a robust numerical basis for simulation studies and potentially aiding in the identification of mechanical abnormalities within the heart.

This research paper investigates the relationship between the spread of a population of particles following linear diffusion laws and an exponential distribution of a physical property, such as permeability. A newly developed technique, based on fitting power-law functions to the midpoints of a histogram, enables estimation of the diffusion coefficient and the fractal dimension of a property's distribution from a single histogram. The technique's reliability has been verified through Monte Carlo simulations with known parameters. The estimated parameters from simulated data match the expected values within narrow margins. The technique's utility in determining parameter values from histogram data has been further explored with varying initial conditions and field strengths. The expected relationship between the spread of a population and a physical property, such as diffusion coefficient and the distribution of permeability, is nonlinear but predictable. The non-linear relationship between these parameters allows for multiple mechanisms of diffusion competition, leading to diverse population distributions that may exhibit non-normal diffusion. The predicted mechanisms of diffusion competition, resulting from the spread of a physical property, include multiple-diffusion-tail, multiple-diffusion-power-law, and multiple-diffusion-logarithmic scenarios, each associated with a specific distribution of the property, such as an exponential, power-law, or log-normal distribution. The theoretical model provides a framework for understanding the complexity of non-Fickian diffusion by accounting for the distribution of a physical property that influences the spread of a population of particles, rather than considering diffusion as an intrinsic characteristic of an individual particle.

The classical electrodynamic interplay, both linear and Kerr nonlinear, between a optical resonator and a waveguide is modeled. This involves transforming Maxwell's equations into a set of coupled differential equations that define a system's state space, which is subsequently linearized for small field intensities. By applying an adiabatic approximation, a set of discrete mode coefficients is obtained, which is further simplified to involve only two primary coefficients after considering the adiabatic nature of a idealized optical resonator and waveguide.

A/reverse modeling of complex fluid dynamics, also known as flow, poses significant challenges due to its inherently chaotic and sensitive nature to even minimal changes or data noise. To restore high-fidelity flow fields from incomplete measurements, a generative adversarial network was developed, resulting in a novel model called PhysX2ResNet. This innovative framework combines a physics-informed partial convolutional encoder with a resNet-based generator and discriminator to achieve accurate flow field restoration. A key feature of PhysX2ResNet is its reliance on low-resolution flow fields, constructed from characteristic flow patterns such as recirculation zones, shock structures, and vortex shedding frequencies, which can be easily identified through flow field visualization and Strouhal number analysis at various Reynolds numbers. A comprehensive comparison was conducted between PhysX2ResNet and its counterpart, PhysResNet, demonstrating that PhysX2ResNet offers notable improvements in restoration accuracy for external flow scenarios, including flow around a sphere with Reynolds numbers of 470 and 4700, as well as flow around an airfoil with a rectangular tab at the trailing edge with a range of Reynolds numbers.

The application of artificial intelligence in game environments has been positively received, yet the ongoing complexity of reinforcement learning algorithms' assessment remains an ever-shifting challenge. As novel algorithms are constantly developed, rigorous evaluation is essential to ensure continuous progress. Unfortunately, current methods of testing are increasingly labor-intensive and prone to errors. To mitigate this issue, we introduce L2Explorer, an automated framework for reinforcement learning algorithm evaluation that enables the seamless integration of newly developed models and facilitates comprehensive studies across multiple models and datasets. The L2Explorer framework is versatile, allowing for the expansion of existing models in a straightforward manner. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we applied the system to the game Super Glue, and released it publicly for the benefit of the research community. We invite the community to utilize L2Explorer for their own studies and contributions.

In order to make process-oriented applications more beneficial, it's crucial to improve the surveillance and exploration capabilities of processes. This can be made easier with the assistance of debuggers and analyzers. However, existing methods for concurrency debugging and process analysis largely assume a fixed point in time for the system under investigation, which limits their applicability when dealing with highly concurrent systems. Existing process exploration tools and validators for process algorithms fail to accommodate dynamically changing data. This paper proposes a new, dynamic surveillance method for declarative processes that rely on data streams, which can be made safer and more efficient with the integration of validators and explorers. This approach assumes that processes are specified using logic programming and that the considered executions are result streams. This can be seen as part of the broader research into concurrency debugging in answer set programming and prolog programming. This paper explores the limitations of existing concurrency explorers and validators in answering the following questions: can they correctly identify conflicts and invariants in declarative processes; can they explore all possible solutions; can they correctly identify sources of non-determinism; can they visualize processes effectively; and can they handle processes with dynamically changing data.

The paper provides a comparison between two methods for determining the dimension of the compactification of the parameter space Sp(m,n). First, by utilizing Erwan Coster's findings, the algebraic dimension is determined as $\begin{cases} \lfloor \frac{mn}{2} \rfloor & \text{if } n < 2m, \\ \lfloor \frac{m(n-1)}{2} \rfloor + 1 & \text{if } n \geq 2m. \end{cases}$ Secondly, by applying Reynolds and Smith's approach, the analytical dimension is found to be $\dim \check{Sp}(m,n) = \begin{cases} \lfloor \frac{mn}{2} \rfloor & \text{if } n < 2m, \\ \lfloor \frac{m(n+1)}{2} \rfloor - 1 & \text{if } n \geq 2m. \end{cases}$ The derived dimensions are then contrasted with existing results from various sources, highlighting both consistencies and discrepancies depending on the relationship between n and m.

Using star formation rate measurements from "z-CAT" and mass functions from SPIDR, we examined the connection between a galaxy's total mass and its star formation rate, particularly for early-type galaxies (ETGs). For ETGs, we observed that this relationship breaks down around a total mass threshold of $10^{10.2}M_{\sun}$ at higher redshifts ($z > 2$). This indicates that ETGs form stars more actively than other galaxies at these elevated redshifts. By analyzing the relationship for disk galaxies and separating it into bulge and disk components, we found that all galaxy bulges follow the same star formation limits as external galaxy limits. However, there is very little low-mass star formation allowed for these galaxies at $z > 2$. We also discovered a correlation where the break in the mass-star formation relationship shifts to the left for galaxies with greater total masses. This suggests that the relationship is driven by the balance between gravitational forces and gas pressure support. Ultimately, our study suggests that the pressure support in galaxies plays a crucial role in shaping their behavior across different scales, and that the super-starburst region may be where the most significant star formation occurs in galaxies with massive bulges.

A cross-linguistic sentiment evaluation model that leverages shared knowledge
to predict sentiment in one language based on the sentiment in another. This
study aims to address this challenge by utilizing multi-task learning,
reflecting real-world scenarios where available data in both languages is
limited. By training a neural network on multiple related sentiment
prediction tasks simultaneously, the study shows that the model performs
better than one that does not use shared knowledge.

Based on the data from ICU patients infected with COVID-19, X-ray images were processed using a hybrid approach combining the Otsu method and the Curvature filter to detect and segment lesions, curating 540 images for further analysis through Support Vector Machine (SVM). While SVM achieved a high accuracy of 92%, it failed to support the hypothesis that visual patterns in X-ray images could distinguish ICU infections from mild infections.

The concept of a simplicial bundle over a space X has two distinct interpretations. 
The first interpretation involves the existence of a simplicial space that mirrors the 
simplicial properties of X along with additional features. 
The second interpretation comprises a mapping f from the total space of the bundle 
to X, exhibiting specific characteristics. 
This paper concentrates on the global simplicial bundle over X, demonstrating the 
existence of a distinct category of simplicial spaces. 
The concept of a simplicial structure serves as an alternative representation, 
offering a means to reconstruct the original simplicial space. 
The term "simplicial structure" is inspired by the corresponding definition for 
"group structures". 
The simplicial approach is akin to a group structure, enabling the replication of 
certain expected properties.

This paper delves into the challenge of erroneous positive associations in the visual association detection (VAD) task. A common real-world application of VAD is leveraging social media images to identify the people within them. A primary difficulty in this application is the frequent generation of erroneous positives, where the system incorrectly identifies the individuals depicted. For instance, a photo of the Eiffel Tower may lead to the erroneous association of a famous French model. To address this problem, our approach incorporates a simple yet effective strategy that integrates external knowledge about locations into the VAD training process, under the assumption that locations can provide contextual clues about the people present. Our method refines visual association models by leveraging location information as a supplementary feature. Through in-depth investigations using a newly created dataset, our model achieves substantial improvements in reducing the number of erroneous positive associations when evaluated with a proposed metric.

We are investigating a galaxy at approximately 3 billion years old, belonging to a cluster, which exhibits characteristics of a low mass spiral and a developing bulge. This galaxy, located in the Coma cluster and named Com/XXI, displays a 2.5kpc bulge with a high star formation rate and exhibits a significant amount of old, metal-rich stars. In contrast, the outer parts of the galaxy consist of younger, less metallic material. Utilizing spectral data from the SPHEREx project, we are exploring the potential for an early accretion event that impacted the outer regions of the galaxy, resulting in increased turbulence that facilitated the migration of a substantial bulge through radiative heating. We are also considering an alternative explanation that connects the two phenomena directly. Both theories may help us understand how galaxies and their surrounding clusters evolve and interconnect.

On November 7, 2004, a particularly powerful solar flare occurred at location 469 and classified as a 2.5 class X-ray event. This flare gave rise to high-energy particles and subsequently a neutron burst observed on the ground. A in-depth analysis was conducted on solar neutron data from two space agencies, ROSAT and SOHO, located at different angles relative to the flare's position. A theoretical model of particle production was applied to interpret these observations. This model indicated that high-energy particles, specifically electrons and ions of various charges, influenced the formation of neutrons. A key discovery was that a heavy ion, with an energy level of 80MeV/nucleon (identified as sulfur), was detected for the first time in a solar burst.

The discovery of exoplanets by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite continues, with over 3000 confirmed planets from its data, including some that are "hot Jupiters" with extremely low densities. The extremely short rotation periods of these hot Jupiters, typically around 10 hours, are contrary to expectations, given the high temperatures near their stars should cause significant atmospheric winds, resulting in higher rotation speeds. In an attempt to explain this phenomenon, several factors such as interactions between the gas giant and its host star, as well as magnetic fields, were considered. The primary hypothesis, suggesting that star-planet interactions could slow down a planet's rotation by applying torque, is particularly intriguing, as it may indicate that the excess atmospheric heat observed on these planets is absorbed rather than generated internally. Theoretical models of angular momentum interactions between stars and planets were also explored to further support this hypothesis, with the exception of one model predicting that rotation speeds would increase, which appears counterintuitive given the excess heat sources present within the planets.

The rapid proliferation of news and video content on the internet has given rise to a rampant problem of counterfeit media, which has serious societal implications.  Effective counterfeit news detection is crucial, however, existing methods struggle due to the lack of structured information and the diversity of content on the internet.  In order to tackle this challenging task, our approach is inspired by the concept of emergent behavior and we propose a novel meta neural process model for multimodal counterfeit news detection.  This approach enables the emergence of shared latent features from a small amount of data by learning instance-specific and generalizable representations for each content modality.  In addition to emerging latent features, we design a cross-modal attention mechanism to effectively fuse the learned representations for each content modality.  Our model is evaluated on two large-scale real-world datasets and it significantly outperforms baseline methods in terms of detection accuracy.  In particular, our approach achieves a new state-of-the-art performance on the ememge dataset with a F1-score of 0.755 and a click-through rate of 0.15, outdoing the previous best result by a margin of 0.033.  Furthermore, our model demonstrates strong generalizability and it ranks second in the second Neural Process benchmark, generalizing from unseen domains with minimal data.  To generalize our approach to a wide range of tasks and domains, we develop a few-shot learning framework that effectively leverages the emerging latent features learned by our model

This research paper examines how solutions to a recurrent transport equation change under variations in initial conditions, focusing on the impact of a sub-sequence of times $t_n$ where these variations are nearly non-decreasing functions. It is shown that there exists a specific sequence $t_n$ that results in at least a sudden, first-order discontinuity in the function $\rho_{t_n}$, regardless of how smooth they may be. Furthermore, the concept of a "recurrent transport" is introduced, along with its relationship to classical and random transport processes.

The concept of Golay complementary structures (GCS) was first introduced by Stark in 1967 to enhance the signal processing capabilities of radar and sonar systems. A significant improvement was later achieved by Koml\'os in 1974, formulating a sequence design that is now referred to as the Koml\'os-Tototh (KT) GCS, which consists of two sequences with lengths in a 1:2 ratio. These designs are highly efficient as they combine three phases, allowing a substantial increase in processing efficiency compared to previous methods. The paper explores the properties of the KT GCS, providing an in-depth analysis of their mathematical structure and potential applications in signal processing.

This research investigates in-depth the electron and nuclear spin behavior in silicon vacano-molecular structures, specifically silicon vacano-dimers on silicon surfaces, presenting an in-depth understanding. By analyzing various spectra of these models, researchers have identified long-range magnetic interactions between electron and nuclear spins as well as extensive electron electron interferences. Furthermore, researchers have demonstrated the feasible transfer of both electron and nuclear spins across a specific surface, setting the stage for potential applications in quantum information processing.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been highly effective in various network analyses and classifications. However, traditional GNN approaches struggle to incorporate dynamic information due to their reliance on aggregate features, which may lead to biased learning. In response, this paper introduces a novel framework that combines dynamic and static data in an attention-based Graph Neural Network (AttnGNN). We then apply this AttnGNN framework to design a fully dynamic architecture-learning model (AttnGNN-A) for time-series forecasting and system failure prediction. Experimental evaluations on diverse real-world datasets, including the aviation system and COVID-19 propagation networks, demonstrate that our methods consistently outperform existing state-of-the-art techniques.

In the context of homotopy theory, a specific type of structure known as a combinatorial 3-category of symmetric sequences is examined, which comprises various partitioning combinations under the principles of concatenation and the exchange of components. A detailed exploration of this structure's underlying compositional semantics is conducted, particularly in relation to the associativity and symmetry of its constituent parts. By analyzing its homotopy-theoretic properties, a fundamental connection between two previously unrelated concepts of partitioning is revealed, namely, the association between non-associative concatenation and the rearrangement of components based on the symmetry of partitions.

Generating realistic cerebral lesions on normal CT images is a common practice to expand datasets for training deep learning models in detecting and diagnosing brain disorders. However, manually creating lesions is time-consuming and inefficient. Although previous methods using generative models to generate lesions have expanded datasets, many of these images did not accurately reflect the characteristics of real cerebral disorders and were not suitable for training detection algorithms. Furthermore, many generated images were based on simple geometric shapes rather than realistic lesions. In this study, a novel progressive neural network was developed using a generative model to generate cerebral lesions that preserve anatomical bone structures while maintaining the accuracy needed for brain lesion detection. We evaluated this approach by comparing it to other techniques and manually generated lesions in terms of anatomical structure preservation, and the results showed that our progressive model produced more realistic lesions with better anatomical preservation. The generated data can be used to pre-train detection algorithms, extending their applicability to a wider range of tasks.

GP 2 is a graph-based language designed for high-performance computing systems, leveraging graph supercomputers with unprecedented scalability. While easy to use, its performance-critical nature requires low-level optimizations typically beyond the reach of its average user base. Previous attempts at improving GP 2's efficiency, including a custom compiler, have yielded limited success due to the constraint of graph algorithms' fixed execution flow. To address this, a new compiler has been developed that exploits parallelism at instruction level, enabling significant performance gains. This compiler achieves up to a 6 times faster performance compared to its predecessor, a 4 times faster than a previous version, and is now integrated into the GP 2 distribution for user benefit.

Recently, external resources like knowledge graphs, KIF tables, and various attributes have fueled the progress in artificial intelligence systems for natural language handling. Although they are typically developed individually and for particular purposes, there is an growing requirement to create language protocols capable of integrating multiple types of external resources. However, current methods in creating these resources are inconstant, with some extracting significant but overlapping language elements, leading to redundancy and making it difficult to examine and manage the relationships between these elements. In response to this issue, we present a novel unified framework that employs contrastive learning to identify and connect various forms of external resources, ensuring each component is distinct yet easily convertible into one another. Experimental results demonstrate that our model successfully differentiates between entities, attributes, and events, and shows that the events extracted by our model's unified framework produce better performance in classification tasks when compared to previous methods. In addition, we found that the framework can also enhance the precision of question generation when applying it to convert entities into questions and events into questions.

This research paper focuses on creating information quotient groups, specifically examining semi-direct and twisted semi-direct product groups acting on a set. We also investigate the properties of these information quotient groups in relation to their associated Cayley graphs and twisted Cayley graphs. By studying maximal star normal subgroups within a twisted wreath product $G \wr_{\tau} K \perm A$, we can derive new insights about the twisted symmetric group when certain conditions are met. We have discovered new infinite collections of star normal quotient networks for both Cayley graphs and their twisted versions.

Handling high-dimensional categorical data is crucial in a wide range of applications, and we introduce a novel group sparsity penalty to effectively select groups of categorical variables. We name this penalty as the Group Lasso-DCP, and it incorporates both the L2-norm and a new "number of binary digits" norm to measure the size of continuous and categorical variables, respectively. The number of binary digits norm minimizes the number of encoded binary variables, and we prove that this penalty complies with the irreducibility and invertibility principles that are vital for categorical variable analysis. The Group Lasso-DCP is applicable to both generalized linear models and neural networks, and we develop an effective proximal gradient method to solve this challenging optimization problem. We further demonstrate that this method can leverage the group-sparse structure to significantly accelerate convergence, and we establish multiple convergence rates for various models, including the logistic regression with neural networks. To visualize the model coefficients, we propose a new visual lasso plot, and we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach using synthetic and real data sets, showing its capability to recover true model sparsity and outperform existing methods, even in high-dimensional scenarios. We provide an R package to make this method accessible to a broader audience, and we discuss potential future research directions.

Dense sparsity patterns in large language models (LLMs) result from the pruning process, which虽能提高推理速度和降低内存占用, 但在某些应用场景中会限制功能。为克服这一问题，我们提出了一种称为结构化稀疏洞察 infusion (SKILL) 的技术，可在不丢弃有用连接的情况下，为现有模型注入额外的稀疏模块。通过将这些模块与主模型组合并采用灵活的网关机制，我们能够精确控制信息的流动，将子模型仅激活于特定任务子集。通过多个评估，我们显示了将单纯前向传播的 SKILL 架构与基于训练的网关机制相结合，能在各种自然语言处理任务和模型规模上显著提升性能。 furthermore, 我们揭示了模型剪枝所带来的缺陷，以及通过 STAIR 技术可以如何弥补这些缺失。

This paper addresses the issue of lines undergoing spatial anti-aliasing when drawn between map points, a problem exacerbated by high-resolution displays and mobile devices. As the underlying coordinate system of vector maps is inherently precise, even minimal discrepancies between adjacent points can lead to unrealistically detailed renditions. To mitigate this challenge, we present and discuss three potential solutions, each with varying levels of effectiveness, before presenting case illustrations and concluding with summary remarks.

To enhance the quality of speech on specific devices with damaged audio, a model is proposed that combines two types of speech processing modules - a dual-path feature extraction component and a recurrent speech reconstruction component. This hybrid model has been shown to achieve superior performance in a speech enhancement task compared to previous approaches, particularly when in the form of an asymmetric two-layer version.

To advance multi-fluid modeling of atmospheric phenomena like storms, this research proposes a step-change from single-column models that incorporate buoyancy effects, typically used for validating multi-fluid approaches. By employing the newly developed multi-fluid solver Kershaw-Arakawa-Lau (KAL) scheme, conventional understanding of Rayleigh-Benard convection is explored via a single-column simulation. Initially, a two-fluid model with negligible horizontal variations demonstrates negligible benefit over the standard single-fluid model. However, when vertical inhomogeneity is introduced, the KAL scheme exhibits its advantage in accurately capturing the distribution of the upper fluid species. Conically shaped convection currents emerge in the two-fluid model, mirroring vertical heat transport patterns observed in the single-fluid model. Notably, the heat transport in both models follows the $Ra^{-1/3}$ scaling law, but the two-fluid model displays skewed probability distributions of local Rayleigh numbers. These findings provide valuable guidance for anticipating multi-fluid model performance in atmospheric applications, where horizontal inhomogeneity is prevalent.

Within the framework of three Jaynes-Cummings models in sequence, we investigate the entanglement generation capabilities of three isolated Jaynes-Cummings systems (JCS). Each system consists of a two-level atom and a harmonic cavity that has no initial phase relationship with the others. We analyze how the interaction parameters within each JCS and the entanglement within the system impact the ability to generate and distribute quantum entanglement between the atoms, specifically in cases where the atoms are not fully entangling within the JCS due to strong interactions. We identify a range of parameters that allow for the safe transfer of at least some degree of entanglement to a distant atom, regardless of whether the intermediate JCS is entangling or not. We find that there is a minimum amount of entanglement within the JCS that is necessary to successfully exchange with a distant atom, as well as a set of parameters that can fully exchange entanglement with the distant atom from specific JC states.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
the prediction of real-world events and the anticipation of emerging trends.
This study presents a method based on recurrent neural networks, specifically using
long short-term memory, to perform sentiment analysis on Twitter data.
This approach overcomes the limitations of traditional probabilistic patterns that
rely on hand-crafted features and positive/nounoun bigram patterns.
This study also establishes a comprehensive set of 10,000 events for which
a positive or negative sentiment can be inferred from Twitter content.
To further test the effectiveness of our method, we conducted a survey involving
180 volunteers to gather individual-level sentiment data on 1,000 current events.
This approach reveals that our method outperforms previous approaches, with results
showing a significant improvement in accuracy, specifically with F-scores of 0.835
and 0.8 for classifying positive or negative sentiment on Twitter content for
news articles and Wikipedia pages, respectively.

A nonlinear interaction in a four-dimensional anti-De Sitter spacetime leads to the formation of charged black holes, and as a result, they exhibit shadow images and satisfy the weak gravitational conjecture, with the goal of outlining this relationship in the context of these black holes.

An in-depth investigation is conducted to determine how the nonlinear charge parameter, the angular momentum, and the charge of the black hole influence the size of the shadow and the arc length of the charged black hole's shadow image, and the interplay between these factors are mapped out.

Gravitational conjecture requires that the charge of the black hole not exceed a specific limit related to its mass and the angular momentum, and beyond this limit, results in unstable orbits that prevent the formation of shadow images.

Additionally, a set of graphs and shadow images are generated to provide a more accessible reference for the study of charged black holes in a nonlinear interaction in an anti-De Sitter spacetime.

Reconstructing the density matrix of nonstationary systems can be achieved using the tomographic method, which has been examined for its ability to display quantum phenomena such as entanglement and Bell inequality violation. These features are most clearly visible in Bibeault diagrams, which provide a visual representation of tomographic reconstructions and highlight areas where a Bell inequality is violated by coloring them differently. This approach was applied to analyze a system consisting of two quantum dots coupled with a collective reservoir, exhibiting nonmonotonic patterns of entanglement and time-dependent Bell inequality violation.

360-degree video is becoming widely used in video streaming services and virtual reality experiences. Due to the large data size of 360-degree video, it is impossible for viewers to view the entire video at once, and they must navigate the video to find the important content. Content-based viewport forecasting technology can help viewers efficiently traverse video by predicting which parts of the video are likely to be viewed. While research has been conducted on 360-degree video forecasting, it is limited to static videos where viewers remain in place. In this paper, a novel framework is proposed to forecast viewports for 360-degree travel videos, where viewers move through a 360-degree virtual environment. A subtitle-based content representation is utilized to effectively capture the dynamic video content, and two forecasting models are developed within the proposed framework. The first model is based on the assumption that viewers follow their interests and are influenced by their immediate field of view and predicted subtitles within their current viewport and surrounding views. The second model leverages graph neural networks to capture long-range dependencies and forecast viewports accordingly. The proposed framework has been evaluated on a real-world dataset, and the results show that it significantly outperforms the baseline methods.

The research aimed to enhance the efficiency of tensor network representations for 1D central critical systems in a thermal state or undergoing dynamic evolution. Initially, we determined precise relationships between system parameters and tensor network properties, specifically the bond dimension and numerical entropy. These relationships allowed us to systematically produce tensor network models that accurately represented thermal states and dynamic developments. To achieve this, we developed an innovative strategy combining previously established methods, resulting in a systematic approach to creating optimized tensor network models. Our research also revealed new, previously unexplored precise relations for the entropy bond dimension relationship in both ground state and thermal/state-evolved conditions. Furthermore, the developed construction strategy was successfully applied to various models, including those with Hamiltonians lacking conserved numbers, and provided a potentially universal description of the high-temperature entropy divergence.

We develop a decoupling theory for functions on the paraboloid in $\mathbb{R}^n$ by introducing a measure of "restricted effectiveness" that reflects the degree to which individual components of a function's support contribute to its norm. This concept is inspired by elements of sparse harmonic analysis. We show that functions with low restricted effectiveness can have their local and global norms compared with a high power loss, in contrast to the standard decoupling approach that results in a loss proportional to the dimension. This offset is part of a function that grows more slowly than any polynomial of positive degree. This method of "through decoupling" is applied to obtain improvements in estimates related to the decoupling of functions on the paraboloid.

The position of the first infrared renormalon singularity in the Borel plane is a critical feature of certain hadronic processes, which are affected by power corrections of $\mathcal {O}(\lambda \, x_{\mathrm{T}}\, x_{\mathrm {B}})$. In high-energy particle collisions at the LHC, particularly in forward particle production involving proton-nucleus interactions, a detailed study of a color dipole transverse momentum distribution revealed its Borel transform to have a non-zero moment, indicating an intrinsic scale of $\lambda \, x_{\mathrm{T}}\, x_{\mathrm {B}}\,\mathrm {GeV}$. This implies an inherent limitation of interpreting TMD PDFs through a perturbative expansion. As a result, any meaningful analysis of TMD PDFs requires an intrinsic scale that typically varies for different hadrons.

Using a two-color femtosecond laser to simultaneously irradiate an metallic lattice at a mirror-coated interface with a dielectric, we achieve vector-controlled surface electron gas gauge fields through controlled orthogonal lattice mismatches. Our method overcomes the limitation of conventional lattice models, where monochromatic surface lattice models produce vector-average gauge fields that favor one direction over the other. By vector-manipulating the vector-sensitivity of the photonic lattice model with varying intensities, we create a unique standard for controlling surface lattice dynamics.

The decision support system (DSS) has gained considerable interest in the field of
artificial intelligence due to its ability to support users by making decisions
based on various inputs. A prominent example of a decision-based DSS is the
Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) solver, which determines the shortest possible
route for visiting a given set of cities. A catalyst for developing efficient TSP
algorithms was the 1933 TSP contest organized by the German Operations Research
society. The contest's goal was to identify algorithms that could solve 50 real-
world instances, comprising 22 cities each. What set the 50 TSP examples apart
was their decision-neutral nature, meaning they were devoid of any bias towards
particular solutions. It was this decision-neutral characteristic that inspired
the creation of black-box frameworks, specifically designed to develop efficient
TSP-algorithms in a generalizable manner. A black-box framework would take input
in the form of a set of cities, determine a shorter route based on their current
ordering, make a decision whether to keep the current route or not in a decision
boundary, and ultimately classify the set of cities into two groups: those that
warrant a shorter route and those that do not. Despite their effectiveness, all
current examples of black-box frameworks, including ours, were tailored to specific
TSP instances and were not designed to be versatile across a wider range of problems

We studied $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decays, and also observed, with some confidence, $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decays for the first time.
Confirmed $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ decay rate is $2.10\pm 0.46$ picobarns, and $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ decays were found at a rate of $0.65\pm 0.38$ picobarns.
These results are for $B^0_s$ mesons with a certain momentum and are directly comparable to previous results from other experiments.

Constructing the lattice of submodules of a given module is a fundamental issue in abstract representation theory. Given a module with a set of submodules that forms a lattice under specific relationships, can we deduce the lattice of submodules of the underlying module? Under the condition that a given module is a direct sum of lattice modules with mutually orthogonal lattices, can we construct its lattice of submodules? This paper is based on a presentation at LATTICE 2020, where these questions are explored and relevant research is presented.

This research focuses on developing a shared behavior model for multiple robots executing the same task, leveraging individual robot-specific observations. By utilizing neural networks, our approach enables each robot to independently learn from its own experiences, facilitating cooperation and shared understanding without requiring cross-training or specialized agents. We highlight the benefits of such a model in cooperative scenarios, demonstrating its superiority over baseline methods through rigorous testing on both made-up and real-world tasks, including an intricate box-pushing task involving multiple robots.

Personalized codes, often abbreviated as PAC codes, were introduced by
Doering and Wagner with the main purpose of distinguishing legitimate users
from attackers in Intra-Interpose protocol. To fully leverage the performance
of Intra-Interpose, a comprehensive understanding of the PAC code characteristics
is necessary. This paper provides an in-depth analysis of PAC codes, comparing
them to well-studied codex families. We also develop an efficient method,
referred to as the Computation of PAC codes (CPAC), for calculating their error-
correcting capabilities and average Hamming distance. Furthermore, we integrate
the Intra-Interpose protocol into the BGP and present Intra-Interpose over BGP
(I2B), which enables a large-scale assessment of Intra-Interpose on hundreds or
even thousands of devices. Our cpac algorithm, implemented within I2B, demonstrates
a significant improvement over previous measurement techniques by offering a more
accurate and efficient way to determine PAC code characteristics. This in turn
allows for a meaningful evaluation of the error correction performance of
Intra-Interpose across various codex families and scenarios. Experimental
results obtained through I2B on a set of around 2.5 million pairs from a single

Neural machine translation (NMT) models typically generate translations sequentially, where each word is dependent on the previous ones, an process that often leads to errors especially with long translations. We investigated the benefit of generating entire translations at once using extensive action space reinforcement learning for guiding the model, drawing inspiration from natural language generation guidance in natural language processing. We guide the NMT model using simple, human-like evaluation metrics such as BLEU, which lead to improved performance over traditional training methods. Our model demonstrates superior results on standard NMT benchmarks, particularly for sentences with longer lengths.

The study of how systems far from thermal equilibrium reach a non-equilibrium steady state (nss) is compelling. In this study, we investigate the feasibility and characteristics of a unique, time-dependent drive that allows a two-level quantum system to reach a steady state while being subjected to interactions with an environment. We examined the driven two-level system dynamics under various conditions, including different drive frequencies, driving amplitudes, decay rates, and coupling to the environment. Theoretical methods used to study this system include a perturbation expansion and numerical simulations. The results show that a steady state can be reached for this system, with distinct features compared to constant driving conditions. The expression for the steady-state population of the excited state is derived, allowing for an optimized condition to be determined. Theoretical findings are validated through experimental data.

We provide the generalized equational framework for biharmonic hypersurfaces deniated by two recurring operators within the Euclidean space. This framework encompasses and expands upon various earlier findings for both submanifaces and sub-Lagrangianianian hypersurfaces. A specific outcome of this framework involves the characterization of all submanifaces that satisfy $ \Delta \Delta \mathcal{K} = 0 $, confirming that they comprise either complete minimal submanifaces or harmonic functions over minimal submanifaces. This result is a substantial extension of previous results limited to the Euclidean space. A comprehensive proof is offered for all stated equational statements.

A collection of positive integers is said to be p/q-identifiable if, given access to a unknown integer from the collection, another integer can also be determined within a factor of p/q based on knowledge of the unknown integer. This concept builds upon the previously established q-identifiable collections. The primary objective of this research is to characterize collections that are p/q-identifiable for any given p/q ratio greater than 1. This in turn characterizes q-identifiable collections. Furthermore, this level of detail is achieved by examining collections with specific properties, including those related to polynomial growth, and comparing them to collections that are q-identifiable.

NoSQL databases, including MongoDB, are gaining popularity for large-scale data management due to their scalability and flexibility. However, they compromise on certain ACID properties, particularly transactional integrity. This research proposes a framework to ensure the reliability of MongoDB transactions by detecting anomalies. The framework monitors transactions at the application level, using minimal overhead and not requiring changes to existing code. It can identify problematic transactions caused by various issues, including bugs, system failures, and data inconsistencies resulting from non-transactional operations. The proposed framework was applied to ensure the transactional integrity of MongoDB for a voting service prototype and a Twitter-like application, demonstrating its effectiveness in catching and preventing issues that threaten transactional integrity.

We demonstrate that a specific set of coefficients, associated with a non-commutative polynomial, are naturally in one-to-one correspondence with the coefficients of a normalized chromatic symmetric function for a particular graph, leading to their inherent positivity. This result is achieved by defining an inverse Kostka tableau based on the non-commutative scalar type monomials. This approach extends the established $e$-positivity of the chromatic symmetric function for complete bipartite graphs. Furthermore, we establish the inherent $s_\alpha$-positivity of the chromatic symmetric function for complete $k$-partite graphs, with equal partition sizes, for any integer $k$ greater than or equal to 3, by proving the $s_{\alpha_{rational}}$-positivity of the Littlewood-Richardson coefficients. This latter property is a known inherent positive property of the Littlewood-Richardson coefficients.

A study was conducted on a specific type of hidden network structure, known as "concealed geometry," in isolated nanoscale assemblies of tetrauclear $Cu_4$ molecules, which exhibit magnetic properties. These assemblies contain a combination of direct and triangle-based connections between individual copper ions, which were found to conceal a tetrahedral geometric arrangement. Utilizing various experimental techniques, including neutron diffraction, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and magnetic resonance, researchers were able to determine the precise arrangement of the molecules and their intricate internal and external geometric configurations. By applying computational simulations, researchers were able to better understand how the concealed geometry, along with the different types of magnetic interactions occurring between the copper ions, influenced the system's overall magnetic properties. This study provides valuable insights into how hidden network structures can be harnessed to engineer the magnetic properties of nanoscale materials, potentially paving the way for novel applications in quantum information processing and nanotechnology.

The inner heliosphere is influenced by external forces, such as those from galaxies, the local interstellar cloud, and the sun, whose contributions to the local interstellar environment are being investigated using data from the Parker Solar Probe. The study focuses on understanding the sun's energy budget in the inner heliosphere, as it is believed to be linked to the size of the supersonic solar wind stream that enters the local interstellar cloud. Understanding this connection is essential for accurately interpreting observations and identifying the mechanism that retains energy, whether it be magnetic reconnection, wave interactions, or magnetic line-tying. The analysis of data from the Interstellar Explorer and Planetary Explorer missions, as well as Parker Solar Probe data, is employed to better grasp the sun's energy budget and its implications for the local interstellar environment. The examination of solar breeze energy components in the inner heliosphere is carried out using data from Parker Solar Probe, as it provides ideal conditions for studying these components due to their distinct features. The analysis reveals that magnetic field energy components are predominant in the inner heliosphere, as indicated by the significant $\beta$ values, and that these components vary along the jet stream, with both thermal and magnetic energy components exhibiting variations both laterally and longitudinally. The findings of this study are visualized through 3D plots, heat maps, and contour maps, as well as statistical analyses, to provide a comprehensive understanding of the sun's energy budget in the inner heliosphere and

This paper delves into the emotional spectrum of human communication, exploring various methods for analyzing and categorizing expressions of joy, sadness, anger, fear, and neutrality among others. The complexity of this task is exacerbated when dealing with speech, particularly when dealing with limited data or uncooperative subjects. Researchers have overcome these obstacles by employing machine learning techniques trained on annotated datasets. The field of speech emotion recognition has since expanded beyond human interactions to encompass a variety of applications. Due to its propensity for overfitting and lack of generalizance, traditional machine learning models struggle to accurately predict emotions in new or unseen contexts. This paper focuses on several innovative approaches that utilize deep reinforcement learning to fine-tune and adapt models across different scenarios and domains. The method presented in this paper entails the development of a novel deep reinforcement learning framework, which leverages an adversarial strategy to adapt models to new contexts or domains. The proposed deep reinforcement learning model is assessed through extensive experiments utilizing well-known datasets, and demonstrates superior performance compared to existing deep learning techniques.

We consider aEXP (expanding pressure) cosmology, and show how a simple, compact object, situated in a spherical cavity that's undergoing expansion, can lead to non-trivial, robust shock waves through non-adiabatic non-ohmic non-linear effects. These results hold true regardless of the equation of state, as a result of the robustness of our model.

Using a substantial $B_s^0$ decay dataset, which requires muonic final states and is from the LEP II data set amounting to 468 million events at an average center-of-mass energy of 91.2 GeV with an energy breadth of 2 GeV, we have studied the form of the $B_s^0\rightarrow D_s^{*-}\mu^{+}\nu_{\mu}$ differential decay rate. A clue-based selection strategy enabled us to directly measure this rate, circumventing the necessity to estimate $B_s^0$ production rates. Our differential decay rate analysis shows that it aligns with the predictions made by the Standard Model, assuming massless $D_s^{*-}$, when fitted using $f_+ (q^2)$ and $f_+ (0)$ parameters. Consequently, we have obtained values of $f_+ (0)$ as $0.334 \pm 0.046 \pm 0.026$ and $0.343 \pm 0.046 \pm 0.026$, where the first uncertainty arises from fitting parameters and the second from cross-section modeling.

A recent paper provides an analysis of advancements made in categorizing monodromy-free one-dimensional Schrödinger operators with periodic potential functions. This monodromy-freedom condition is equivalent to ensuring that all energy levels within a particular band edge are highly degenerate. An approach involving generalized orthogonal polynomials satisfying a specific three-term recurrence relationship is developed to determine all potential functions that meet these criteria. An initial formulation of these generalized orthogonal polynomials was introduced by another researcher, and an explicit mathematical proof was given by another group, both of which contribute to the intended study. Ultimately, the intended study involves utilizing the three-term recurrence relationship to determine all generalized orthogonal polynomials within the context of potential functions that exhibit 12-fold symmetry.

During the fracture of materials, scientists have observed an interesting phenomenon known as the "concealed arrangement" that appears in the intensity of sounds produced. This phenomenon has predominantly happened with sample sizes exceeding ten meters but remains unexplained. Now, through the use of a simplified model, researchers have demonstrated that this phenomenon can result from a combination of molecules detaching simultaneously and a phenomenon called resonance. These factors are part of a "crackling universe" that emerges when a layer of material breaks free from a surface. When both the numbers of molecules detaching at the same time and the frequency of their interactions match a particular condition, sound waves get amplified, but only until a specific point is reached. This study provides a framework for understanding the complex behavior exhibited during the cracking of materials.

The concept of an "aether" in QCD is explored, drawing parallels with the "aether" in Einstein-aether theory. It's found that a non-abelian QCD term, of the same order as the temperature, acts as a kind of "aether" term and remains applicable to both linearized and non-linearized interactions with thermal fluctuations. This term is shown to yield finite, non-zero expectations for a variety of otherwise divergent thermal field theory fluctuations. It's also demonstrated that this "aether" influences the thermodynamics and early universe thermal fluctuations of temperature. Additionally, it's proposed that this "aether" term could be observable in thermal fluctuations of the early universe, potentially offering a novel approach to high-precision experimental searches for "aether" theory.

A standard option price incorporates the cost of hedging through the Hahn-Rockafellar theorem, yet this may not fully reflect the actual cost due to potential additional expenses caused by adjusting the hedging strategy in response to market pressures and the trading of collateral at relevant interest rates. In accordance with the EU's Margin Regulation 575/2013, the relevant interest rate is the risk-free rate plus 10.8 basis points (or 11 basis points in the US). In this paper, we demonstrate that through the application of the Itô change of numeraire technique, the equation for the value of collateral required for hedging a portfolio of options can be derived from first principles. Furthermore, the necessity for deriving the collateral requirement from the underlying physics of the process is highlighted, rendering the risk-free rate applicable only in specific circumstances. As a result, an explanatory framework and equation for the valuation of options under dynamic delta hedging and the determination of the collateral rate are presented.

A dynamic prospect equity principle is proposed to address intergenerational inequality. This principle ensures that, across various scenarios and over multiple generations, the sum of the discounted discounted social welfare derived from various prospects equals zero. In a simplified model with an infinite number of generations, this principle equates to the weighted distribution of prospects where the weights are determined by the product of the discount factor and the probability of various pathways in the Markov process that describes the distribution of prospects. This principle is then applied to address the underallocation of opportunities that hampers optimal social outcomes in a environment with unequal opportunities, and it is shown that, in contrast to other equity principles, this principle does not lead to optimal outcomes in such conditions.

The scanlab is a software instrument that adds the capability to automate various measurements using particle accelerators, including measuring the properties of particle beams. This paper describes the beam measurement techniques that use a scan of a beam loss monitor to determine the shape of a beam in transverse space. These methods will be applied in the context of the upgrade to the AD at CERN, but can also be used in other types of particle accelerators.
