Several prominent future experiments, such as the SIMON array, the CMB-S4 small array, and the Cold Electron Relaxation X-band Array, plan to employ superconducting radio frequency kinetic inductance detectors to investigate the cosmic microwave background. To accurately model instrument behavior in this class of experiments, researchers require highly detailed simulations that replicate the specific characteristics of their instruments on a large scale. However, current software tools available for such simulations, including HEALPix, LiTE, and POLCA, lack the necessary functionality to comprehensively simulate these large-scale experiments. In contrast, the s4cmb package was developed to provide an appropriate framework for modeling such scenarios, leveraging the existing tools within its structure. Furthermore, the s4cmb package includes a concrete example of a simulated instrument for the CMB-S4 experiment, which can be utilized as a starting point for researchers designing and building their own experiments.

Recent advancements in natural language processing have been propelled by
pre-trained language models, which have demonstrated remarkable success in various
downstream tasks such as machine translation, translation, and question answering.
However, the way these models represent language has been somewhat enigmatic, leaving
the fundamental functions they perform not fully understood. Using a novel approach, we
seek to illuminate these models' internal operations by examining their role in
reconstructing scrambled sentences. Specifically, we measure the effectiveness of
these models' language preservation capabilities using sentence similarity metrics,
and we discover that even models lacking explicit sentence-keeping training
demonstrate a significant level of language preservation. Moreover, our research
reveals that models' performance improves with the amount of language data they
are exposed to, and that their presence, particularly for more sophisticated models,
could potentially enhance the efficiency of certain NLP tasks by pre-processing
language-related tasks.

For the escalating threat of deepfakes, effective identification methods are crucial. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have produced significant deepfake ideas, yet they often struggle with creating content across multiple domains or user types. In contrast, this paper presents a novel deepfake dataset spanning nine domains with over 200,000 videos, aiming to test and overcome GAN limitations. Furthermore, this paper introduces a new model called MD-CSDNetwork, which leverages knowledge from trained domains to identify deepfakes in new, unseen domains with minimal data. Experimental results show that this approach excels in generalization ability, outperforming state-of-the-art methods on both related and unrelated data sets.

In 1930, mathematician K. Menger developed a comprehensive framework for representing geometric figures as matrices and classified various types of angles. He attempted to emulate this approach for distances but encountered difficulties. This document demonstrates that angles behave similarly to distances in multiple ways, including the strong triangle inequality proposed by Menger, which allows for a structured approach to angle matrices and leads to a systematic classification of all possible configurations, echoing his original goals.

We establish a sequence of iterative approaches to determine the smallest possible value for the residue class field's size, varying in relation to an integer that has a specified property, in relation to the absolute value of the residue of the number field.

The study of a specific polynomial cluster algebra has led to the identification of a cluster structure within the coordinate ring of Bessel polynomials, establishing their universality. Moreover, this discovery enables the definition of a cluster-compatible categorification for a particular part of the quantum $t$-deformation of the positive part of the special linear Lie algebra at a specific angle. The authors further define two distinct categories of cluster-compatible modules over the quantum Bessel algebra and establish an equivalence between these categories at the classical limit.

Forbes highlighted Forsage as the leading pyramid scheme of 2021, with approximately $28 million funneled into the program, yet up to $20 million went to higher-level operators. Despite its high-profile nature, researchers have examined numerous online scams and cyber incidents, there is still a lack of in-depth studies on pyramid schemes. This paper introduces the structure of Forsage, analyzing its entry fees, levels, and revenue sharing model. We reconstructed and made available for use a tool that replicates the Forsage system, enabling the examination of its revenue sharing mechanism. Utilizing this tool, we verified the stated level-7 cap reported in previous work and explored how the pyramid scheme was structured, allowing users to input various data sets and receive visual representations of its composition.

Recent discoveries with the VVV survey have revealed at least five new extragalactic globular clusters in the Local Volume, making it plausible to find at least 19 in the Milky Way's bulge. A study examined 19 GC candidate populations across various galaxies, utilizing color, luminosity, and absorption metrics for further analysis. The researchers employed effective temperature to determine metallicity from the VVV data and found a $0.2$-decade average metallicity difference between the candidate clusters and VVV spectral standards. VVV samples exhibited lower dispersion in metallicity measurements compared to other methods. Furthermore, the study found that globular cluster populations tend to have lower absorption measurements than field star populations, likely compensating for enhanced $ \alpha $-abundances. VVV samples exhibited a $1.5$ K narrower temperature range than previous methods. VVV luminosity functions were analyzed using both non-parametric and parametric approaches, revealing a $1.6$-K temperature difference between the low and high luminosity segments of the VVV luminosity function. Ultimately, a assessment was made of the suitability of using VVV data for globular cluster discovery in various galaxies beyond the Local Volume.

In a significant extension of holographic error correction models with both short- and long-range correlations, a novel approach called hyper-invariant MERA is introduced. The procedure for developing this holographic code is straightforward and can be tailored to incorporate a wide variety of interestng, conformally invariant correlation patterns. When applied to theory that follows the principles of relativity in three spatial dimensions, our hyper-invariant MERA code leads to a two-sided c-theorem that smoothly integrates with its two-particle precursor counterpart. The code also facilitates the study of non-equilibrium many-body dynamics, as well as the analysis of conformal field theory-quantum gravity duality, in a scenario involving a BTZ black hole within a specific time frame.

Deep-learning models such as neural networks and recurrent neural networks have been widely used in analyzing and predicting business process discovery and mining. To advance state-of-the-art process prediction, researchers have incorporated these models. However, a major challenge in using deep-learning techniques lies in explaining and interpreting their decisions. In this study, we investigate the interpretability of these models by employing and comparing reverse inference methods, specifically the inverse problem and the generative approach. Our analysis reveals that the inverse problem provides the most effective interpretation for predicting process variables. Furthermore, our findings show that using a generative approach leads to significant improvements in predicting process behavior accurately. Our research has valuable implications for reverse inference applications in reverse prediction and generation.

We establish key characteristics of two types of function spaces, known as Gelfand-Shilov spaces, in terms of their Fourier transforms. These spaces contain functions that decrease at a rapid rate both at large distances and near the origin. Furthermore, we demonstrate the incompleteness of certain Toeplitz operators, which restrict a polynomial band when applied to these spaces. This incompleteness holds true even in the context of their graph norms.

Sunsimilar star, Ad Leonis (AD Leo) was observed during a huge stellar
outburst in 1985 that significantly increased its brightness across the spectrum,
especially in the near-ultraviolet range. Investigating the physical properties of
AD Leo in the near-ultraviolet during this event presented a challenge due to a
lack of experienced stellar spectra in the near-ultraviolet range. The visible and
infrared emissions could be effectively attributed to a second star, but the
source of the near-ultraviolet brightness remained unclear. Some researchers
proposed that the near-ultraviolet observations were influenced by a dusty disk
around AD Leo, which had previously been detected by infrared imaging. The
current study attempted to simulate the physical properties of this dusty disk to
explain the near-ultraviolet brightness, but this explanation could not be
supported. The study found that even with extremely high albedo values, the dusty
disk's ability to reflect near-ultraviolet light could not account for the
observed emissions. The study also considered the possibility of a hot disk
emitting thermal radiation, but the physical conditions required were extreme
and unlikely. The source of the near-ultraviolet emissions from AD Leo during
this event remains mysterious, although the event offered a rare opportunity to
study the physical properties of a massive, early-stage star.

Our work addresses the limitation of traditional smoothing techniques for point cloud processing, which are often tailored to a specific transformation type. To overcome this issue, we introduce a new framework called TPC that provides smoothing adapted to various transformations for point cloud representations. TPC leverages an adaptive neighbor selection method and a dynamic weighting scheme to dynamically adjust the smoothing process in response to different transformations. Our approach is formulated as a neural network and integrated into existing graph convolutional networks, allowing it to thrive in various downstream tasks. Our key achievement is an 8% improvement in performance on the KITTI dataset for 3D object detection, and we also observe similar performance gains for other 3D object detection and segmentation datasets. To support further research and development, we have made our source code and pre-trained models available online.

This study employs a powerful technique, known as the Jost method, to visualize and better understand the characteristics of the nuclear resonance within the $^{16}$O nucleus. To achieve this, an optical potential is created using the Green's function-based iterative method, then inserted into the Jost formalism to draw a direct connection between the features of the scattering potential and its corresponding eigenfunctions. A unique approach to generating the RPA-based optical potential allows for the incorporation of multiple excitations, leading to a comprehensive and in-depth examination of the quadrupole resonance within the $^{16}$O nucleus. By applying a cutoff to the width of the RPP potential, a complicated structure is uncovered, comprising four distinct components of the resonance: four main peaks and additional smaller portions.

Traditional dimensionality reduction and visualization techniques for dynamical systems rely on geometric structures, yet these features can be obscured or distorted in systems with noisy time series data. In this research, we introduce two innovative methods that utilize external information about expected system behavior to enhance clustering, leading to more reliable results in noisy environments. The first method, known as Data-guided Impact Based (DIB) clustering, utilizes impact maps to create a reduced-order representation of the state space that preserves the geometric structure of attractors. In contrast, our second method, K-guiada Impact Based (I3B) clustering, applies a simpler but effective binning procedure to preserve expected geometric relationships between states. Both methods enable the preservation of expected geometric relationships between states, facilitating more robust and informative clustering even in systems with significant noise levels. We validate the effectiveness of DIB and I3B clustering through numerical simulations of chaotic systems, including a noisy Lorenz attractor, a Lorenz attractor with elevated noise levels, and a Lorenz attractor exhibiting heteroclinic connections.

Generating text is a complex task that large neural networks have been employed to tackle, despite their substantial training parameters. In contrast, networks with sparse structures have historically underperformed in generating language due to limited capacity. In response to these challenges, we introduce SparseGAN, a novel framework comprising a sparse generator and a dense discriminator, which circumvents traditional limitations. By leveraging the strength of a dense network to serve as a discriminator, we can give the generator a critical function in enhancing the representation of text. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the sparse generator can effectively split its responsibilities into a foundational component that hinders the discriminator and a modular component that boosts the representation, both of which are beneficial for text generation. Experimental evaluations on several text generation benchmarks, including those involving language and style translation and controlled generation, indicate the superiority of SparseGAN over existing methods.
The scientific community widely accepts that life on Earth could have been seeded by meteorites containing microorganisms from other parts of the universe.

Telemetry data from recaptured animals can provide valuable insights into the spatial characteristics of a study area, including the location of traps and the presence of alternative food sources. However, traditional capture-recapture models often treat these elements as unknown variables to be estimated, which can lead to area-based models with arbitrary boundaries. In this study, we develop a new statistical model that incorporates the locations of traps and alternative resources into a spatial capture-recapture framework, using a likelihood method. We evaluate the model's fit using simulated data and a real-world dataset collected from brown rats in London, and compare our results to those obtained from an existing package. We also explore various statistical tests to determine the most effective model parameters and test for overdispersion, while considering potential limitations and possible extensions of the proposed approach.

The dynamics of oscillators interconnected through multiple layers are being extensively studied, with a focus on how they influence each other and determine the stability of a synchronized state. In a multilayer environment, we analyze two methods of communication between oscillators: one where information is exchanged within a single layer, and another where information is transmitted across several consecutive layers. Discovering that there are specific conditions under which the method of transmission affects the phase order parameter is a key highlight of our research. Furthermore, our findings can be applied to explain the progression of neuronal activity across the brain's interconnected networks and the spread of opinions in social networks comprised of multiple groups.
A re-formulation of the classical Beltrami equation is achieved by expressing it in terms of the Airy stress function, yielding its minimal parametric representation.

The concept of geometric efficiency, initially proposed by Vazirani and Ta-Shma, has been extended to assess the feasibility of verifying geometric properties for a given algorithm, such as the Geometric Set Intersection method proposed by Vassilev. This framework establishes that the geometric properties underlying the Set Intersection algorithm's efficiency imply a significant improvement over current proof verification methods. Moreover, it has been demonstrated that if these properties provide an efficient means of validation, then fundamental complexity class relationships, specifically $IP=P^{NP}$, would hold. This would, in turn, necessitate that the sets of formulas defining specific geometric shapes, such as semi-algebraic varieties, are undecidable, which is in direct conflict with the fundamental principle of computability.

This paper is a continuing study from previous work with distinctions made for vector behaviors within representations of gl_n over local fields. The nature of these fields, be they characteristic zero or positive, directly influences the representations' characteristics. The primary overview of these relationships will be presented in this paper, along with specific illustrations of those obtained in prior research.

Under network mislabeling malpractice, where graph structures are intentionally distorted, the effectiveness of community detection algorithms is significantly compromised, leading to the production of unreliable and nonsensical classifications. To address this challenge, this paper presents a novel scale estimation method that accurately identifies a graph's community structure parameter under deceptive conditions, enabling the accurate selection of community detection algorithms by providing a reliable indicator of their performance. The proposed scale estimator outperforms existing methods, with experimental results demonstrating its ability to accurately pinpoint graph parameters, thereby facilitating the efficient deployment of community detection algorithms.

This study proposes a novel nonparametric approach for estimating a distribution function based on data collected from vehicles, specifically the empirical vehicle size distribution (EVSD), which is derived from vehicle speeds near a particular location. A key advantage of this method is its nonparametric nature, thereby eliminating the necessity to assume a specific distribution type. The paper constitutes the initial implementation of this technique in the context of traffic applications and proceeds to establish convergence theorems, thereby providing an analytical framework for the approach. The methodology is further enhanced by introducing an estimator that integrates the EVSD with prior information, thereby enriching the methodological toolkit available. A simulation study is conducted to assess the performance of this technique and to determine the optimal conditions for its successful application, thereby providing a comprehensive evaluation of the approach. The paper also includes real-world data analysis using probe vehicle statistics recorded near an intersection in Los Angeles, which serves to illustrate the methodology and its practical relevance. A examination of cumulative distribution functions, vehicle speeds, and road segment characteristics provides a detailed examination of the approach, thereby establishing its credibility and accuracy.

In our latest general relativity simulation software iteration, a few extra integrators for stationary situations have been incorporated to address the needs of researchers working in numerical general relativity. Our primary intent was to fill a gap in existing open-source implementations by developing integrators that satisfy the situation found in many cosmological scenarios with a non-spinning central black hole. The integrators we have implemented serve a purpose beyond this particular case by also addressing the requirements in a few additional situations, specifically those involving binary systems where at least one object is in a binary configuration and possessing multipole properties, as well as a singular quadrupole moment, typically seen in gas disk simulations around black holes. Our integrators utilize a iterative method on the Einstein field equations rather than a conventional numerical solver on the constraint equations, as constraints in stationary scenarios are inherently satisfied when the evolution equations are properly simulated. Our integrators are notable for their robustness and efficiency, as they are nonlinearly convergent, heavily accelerated by a nonlinear solver, and result in computationally efficient simulations that can be completed within a few thousand core hours on a 1000 core system for configurations with up to three black holes and a quark star, in addition to providing precise initial data that significantly reduces simulation instability durations.

Our study investigates the unique "strange" Nernst effect in a semiconductor, exhibiting exceptionally high values that far exceed those observed in metallic systems. This investigation is based on data from the Transverse Thermoelectric Coefficients (ET and RER) in Mn3NiN nitride nanocrystalline film, a novel material with extraordinary thermoelectric and optical properties. The analysis of RER data reveals a migration of an interband gap from 5.2 e in bulk tin dioxide to 3.8 e, potentially indicating a transition from diagonal to vertical character. The investigation of the unusual "strange" Nernst effect reveals peak values exceeding 6000 K between 300 and 500 K, the origin of which is ascribed to the shift of the RER interband gap.

The expansion of the Internet and the rise of Internet-based services have led to the development of large-user centers designed to accommodate both small and massive projects. These centers, which include projects spanning a few gigabytes to exabytes in size, are characterized by their storage capacity, transmission speed, and numbers of concurrent connections. As they are designed to cater to both small- to large-scale projects, these user centers have become environments ideal for investigating the impact of machine intelligence across a wide spectrum of data sizes. This paper presents the architecture and design behind the machine intelligence system deployed at the Earthscope Scientific Center, a high-capacity user center, which is capable of facilitating both single-user and multi-user operations across speeds ranging from megabytes to petabytes.

This paper explores the uniformity of non-autonomous barrier problems under certain growth conditions, building on a framework established by Cardell, De Santa, and Sepulcre. Our analysis includes the uniformity of solutions and level set measures across a range of problem parameters.

This paper offers a simplified proof of key findings established by James and Kwak regarding the structure of certain modules in modular Galois cohomology for GL_2 over p-adic fields. Specifically, we expand on previous work by Omar and explore the modular case of Kummer theory to rederive crucial properties of certain modules, overcoming obstacles posed by the non-commutative nature of our module's ring in contrast to prior research.

We define a constrained measure-to-measure heat flow that is capable of transforming a given non-negative density within a manifold with the property of being minimally embedded. This transformation results in another hypersurface within the same manifold, also minimally embedded. The distance between the two hypersurfaces is reduced in a specific way, considering the fact that the average curvature of the two surfaces remains the same. A new class of regions in a Riemannian space are identified as isothermally embedded with a minimal boundary, representing a combination of isothermal and isoperimetric properties. A constrained version of the isoperimetric problem in a Riemannian space is shown to have a solution that falls into the isothermal-isoperimetric class of regions, provided the constant of mean curvature meets a certain condition in relation to the geometry of the space. A method is developed to approximate any given hypersurface in a way that preserves the mean curvature while reducing its geometric complexity.

This research focuses on identifying the complex electrical permittivity of a self-sensing composite in a specific harmonic frequency to optimize its parameters for effective integration with piezoelectric actuators in impedance matching applications. An improved analytical model is developed to calculate the exact harmonic contour of a self-sensing composite across various shapes and frequencies, providing a reference for experimental validation and optimization. The necessary electromagnetic theory is reviewed and an accurate contour plot of a 5cm x 5cm PZT-5H piezoelectric actuator embedded in a PDMS polymer matrix is derived, validating the theoretical approach and validating the improved model. Furthermore, an iterative process utilizing a genetic algorithm leverages electrical impedance data collected via an electrical impedance tomography system to reconstruct the complex electrical permittivity of the self-sensing composite, confirming its validity and highlighting the importance of having a precise model in the contour.

It was initially thought that combining "less cognitive" component agents would
result in "more cognitive" collective behavior. However, our study challenges this
notion by demonstrating that cognitive proficiency increases in both individual
and collective levels when combining "more cognitive" component agents. By utilizing
"cognitive" measure, comparing ordinary elementally augmented agents (AEAs) to
highly capable elementally augmented agents (HEAEAs), our experimental framework
utilizes a color cognition task to demonstrate that both individual and collective
performance improve when high-capacity AEA and HEAEA groups are combined, but
when low-capacity AEA groups are combined, HEAEA groups exhibit distinctively
astute behavior. Our findings suggest that simple division of labor can lead to
complex cognitive phenomena when incorporating enhanced elemental capabilities.

This research proposes a new way to represent Euclidean space using geometric objects called simplices and their associated algebraic structures. We establish a link between these objects and a specific type of algebraic geometry that captures the properties of Euclidean space. This approach allows us to define a precise geometric interpretation of abstract algebraic structures and in turn, a method to represent these structures in a clearer, more intuitive fashion. This in turn provides a geometric foundation for the abstract structures in question and allows us to derive a relationship between the dimension of Euclidean space and the components that make up our algebraic objects.

The failure of strict diet plans is largely attributed to the unappetizing taste of low-energy food. By consuming scalar or vector low-energy food, which is typically minor in quantity, the taste of regular food could theoretically become enhanced. We highlight the nutritional advantages of such food and analyze how to make it more appealing to eat, focusing on the parameters that could naturally occur and proposing a dietary strategy.

This paper delves into the third-order linear differential equations that are solutions to the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ Toda conformal field theory, establishing an explicit connection with 'twisted' $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ Toda TQ-systems of Kirillov and Reshetikhin. A novel approach is adopted by representing variables as multiplication operators in a specific polynomial space, with the help of which, we identify the universal differential operator whose eigenvalues are variates of interest. Furthermore, we derive an $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ analogue of the famous Opdam-Cherednik formula, demonstrating how the second-highest derivative of this universal operator are eigenfunctions with variates as eigenvalues.
We demonstrate that Coxeter groups possess biautomatic properties, resulting from which we derive that uniform lattices within isometry groups of buildings also exhibit biautomatic structures.

A notable number of studies have been conducted involving individuals with leg amputations in electrocardiogram-based gait analysis studies. This paper presents an approach to identify ambulatory states and calculate step frequencies from electrocorticogram data collected while subjects walked. Step frequencies are calculated using a novel algorithm based on the zero-crossing points of the first derivative of the normalized first principal component. This study involved ten healthy volunteers who walked on a treadmill at different speeds, with their walking speeds ranging from 0.69 to 2.15 km/h, recorded on both legs while standing still and in motion. The results show that the proposed algorithm successfully distinguishes between standing and walking states with high accuracy, with the mean step frequencies closely matching the actual values. There is a slight underestimation of step frequencies, with the corresponding margins being within 0.015 step/frequency. Furthermore, there is a very low correlation between the estimated and measured step frequencies, with a corresponding coefficient of determination close to 0.9985.

Let an RAA group $A$ be defined by a graph $\Gamma$. The goal is to demonstrate that any free subgroup of finite index within $A$ is isomorphic to $A$ itself, which implies that $A$ has no proper subgroups with a finite index. This in property holds true for free groups, which are a subset of RAA groups. The proof of this characteristic being preserved under subgroups of finite index was recently accomplished by Gu\'eritaud and Wise for right-angled groups and can be extended, which utilizes the Stallings foldings technique to establish this result.

In brain imaging research, connectivity analysis is commonly employed to establish relationships between different brain areas. Traditional methods typically focus on efficiency-driven connectivity analysis, but this is limited to pairwise connections. In contrast, sparse and low-rank connectivity models offer a more comprehensive and efficient understanding of interconnectedness among multiple brain regions. However, computing these models can be computationally expensive. In the context of dynamic scenarios, where brain connectivity is analyzed in relation to external factors such as individual differences, it's essential to develop algorithms that are not only accurate but also rapid. In this study, we introduce a new brain imaging model called sparse low-rank efficient connectivity (SLEC), which captures complex, time-varying patterns of brain connectivity by combining sparsity and a low-rank structure. To achieve this, we utilize a variational Bayes approach that maximizes the probability of the model while maintaining a manageable number of parameters. When applied to fMRI resting-state data, the SLEC model demonstrates superior accuracy in predicting interpersonal variations compared to simpler efficient connectivity models.

Understanding how animals move in natural environments is essential in ecological studies. Traditional methods involve capturing animals with measuring tools or by taking videos while they are being held. An alternative approach is analyzing videos where animals are in their natural habitats. This research presents a way to identify the species, measure body length, and track the movement direction of fish from video footage, by using computational techniques. The proposed method can process videos where fish are swimming together, it relies on a fish template that is automatically adjusted to individual scenes, and it produces quantitative measurements of movement.

This research develops a novel iterative method for numerically solving a polynomial equation involving the inverse of a matrix polynomial, leveraging a technique first proposed by Higham for calculating matrix powers. The resulting algorithm can be easily implemented iteratively by utilizing the previous solution as a starting point for the next iteration. A comparison with an existing iterative solver shows that this new method outperforms the alternative, and both algorithms are well-suited for acceleration using GPU technology.

We investigate a one-dimensional Anderson insulator in which an electron is subjected to spatially random binary perturbations of its experience of spatially periodic potential. It was previously shown that such random binary perturbations can induce a topologically nontrivial Hall effect in one dimension. Based on this prior investigation, we derive an effective model that enables the efficient generation of the topological state induced by such random binary perturbations. Furthermore, this effective model permits for an analytical derivation of the Chern number in relation to the strength of the spatially periodic potential.

This work provides a review of the current advancements in polarisation trims and isogeny compositions for generalisations of elliptic curve cryptography systems based on complex structures. The article examines the complexities of combining separable polynomials in the composition of isogenies and compares various methods for combining polarisations in degenerate and non-degenerate cases. The review also explores the application of isogeny compositions in designing more efficient cryptographic protocols. The foundations of these concepts are established in the appendices for a comprehensive understanding.

In the context of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, a specific set of parameter values leads to a physically meaningful, stable vacuum where the Higgs boson remains stable and radiative corrections are manageable. By applying two-loop corrections to the Higgs potential, we have mapped out the conditions under which this desirable behavior occurs and found that it necessitates large left-handed top squark masses in the range of 600-800 GeV/c^2. Without the influence of complex phase effects from CP-violation, our findings on on-shell behavior align with previous research but the complex phase can introduce up to ~5% deviations in the allowed parameter space. When combined with constraints from electroweak symmetry breaking and bottom-quark loop corrections, we estimate the on-shell behavior is feasible within a very narrow window of possible values for several parameters.

This paper delves into the challenges of distributed learning in a common environment, specifically addressing the Multi-Agent Linear Bandit setting with non-i.i.d. data.
It focuses on a new concept - sharing the situational setting - and highlights the difficulty of learning when this condition isn't met, presenting an upper bound of $O(d^{3/2}\sqrt{T+\sum_T n_t N})$.
 The research also presents a more practical upper bound of $O(d^2\sqrt{T+\sum_T n_t N})$ when the number of learning agents and rounds is balanced.
The results demonstrate the feasibility of our proposed multi-agent setup when the situational setting is shared, but proving efficiency when it's not remains an unresolved challenge.

We appreciate the editors and reviewers for their valuable input, which helped us refine the initial version of our paper significantly. Specifically, we addressed concerns raised in Review 3 by refining equation (5) to ensure the data used for estimating the robust loss remained fully independent of the predictions. Moreover, we expanded the discussion in the introduction and appended the discussion on the connection between our approach and that of Wu et al. (2021). This latter discussion, along with additional insights into the choice of $\q$, was moved from the main text to the introduction for better accessibility, and we also incorporated the explanation of the connection to Wu et al. (2021) and other related works, as well as the rationale and effects of the robustness hyperparameter into the discussion section. Additionally, we addressed the issue raised in Review 2 by demonstrating the algorithm's ability to effectively manage at least one additional real-world dataset, and we updated the title of the paper to reflect a JOI.

Our primary goal is to provide precise predictions for inclusive distributions and the elliptic flow coefficient in lead-lead collisions, accounting for initial gluon fluctuations and the influence of the running coupling, as well as the transverse motion of initial particles. Utilizing the Monte Carlo code iGLISSCC in conjunction with the relativistic heavy ion collision code AMPT, we made these predictions for a centrality range of 0-5% and a $p_{\rm T}$ range of 2 to 8 GeV/c in the 2.76 TeV collisions. By comparing our results with ALICE experimental data, we found a reasonable level of consistency across all measured data sets.

When considering an Interference Network with $K$ users, a significant part of the total sum rate region is created by a segment known as the extremal GDoF benefit, which is located between two boundaries defined by throughput guarantees. This segment, however, is limited by two key growth rates that result from both optimal and binary power regulation strategies, denoted as $\beta_{opt}$ and $\beta_{bin}$ respectively, with their difference being $\Delta \beta = \beta_{opt} - \beta_{bin}$. Researchers have previously reported that $\beta_{opt} \approx 1.205\sqrt{K}$ and $\beta_{bin} \approx 0.488\sqrt{K}$, with their difference being $\Delta \beta \approx 0.717\sqrt{K}$ in a network with certain constraints, with analogous results being obtained in unbounded networks. The extremal GDoF benefit, when considering both strategies, is located between $1.693\ +\ \beta_{bin}$ and $1.205\sqrt{K}\ +\ 2$. In contrast, when only taking into account the growth with the number of users, the benefit is found to be between $\beta_{bin}$ and $\beta_{opt}$, with this segment's size being $\Delta \beta$.

This work considers the construction of an efficient numerical integration scheme to accurately model particle collisions in atmospheric processes. A straightforward approach is demonstrated to allow for prolonged interaction between particles, eliminating unnecessary computation in simulated collisions. A simple, adaptable algorithm is proposed to manage interparticle forces over an extended time frame. A volatile liquid model serves as a test case, illustrating a significant improvement in accuracy with this new integration scheme compared to existing methods.

This paper presents four proof methods to establish the existence of integers $a$ and $b$ that satisfy the condition $a^2+ab+b^2=7^k$ for any given positive integer $k$. Furthermore, we provide the following four distinct, equally valid, and independent solutions sets, denoted as $(a_k,b_k)$, which can be derived through respective approaches: congruence theory, Gaussian integers, Euclidean algorithm, and algebraic number theory in the field $\Qp{7}$.

This report describes a model of a one-legged hopping robot consisting of a mass at the end of a spring-loaded shank. The spring mechanism is governed by Hooke's Law, and the other end of the spring is hinged at the ground. The hopping cycle is divided into two main stages: a compression stage where the foot is in contact with the ground, and a restitution stage where the foot propels the robot forward. The equations of motion are solved using the conservation of angular momentum and linear momentum, and the rest angle and restitution angle are calculated. A MATLAB simulation is then conducted to visualize the simulation, and potential improvements are proposed including a directed push-off, a damper, and a longer shank.

A cohesive quark meson scheme is proposed to explain the behavior of quark meson shapes in coherent external fields. This paper focuses on calculating shape factors for quark scalars, vectors, and tensors within a quasiparticle extension of the linear sigma model. Calculations incorporate corrections beyond the tree level using a effective potential that ensures accuracy in determining meson shape factor behavior at zero momentum. Regularization of divergences is handled through a coherent Hamiltonian approach. The paper presents comprehensive analyses of scalar and vector rho-meson mass vector currents and tensor vector currents, and illustrates their relevance by comparing calculated values with experimental data, including the electromagnetic decay of tensor mesons into two vector particles.

In the contemporary dynamic business environment, where the information volume surges at a rapid pace, hierarchical structures have become the prevalent means of organizing and presenting information. The inherent property of hierarchies, where the characteristics of lower-level components contribute to the higher-level entity, facilitates the efficient management and processing of information. This contribution introduces the concept of expandable information models capable of representing hierarchical relationships, building upon the foundational ISA model. The proposed model enables precise calculations and projections of hierarchies based on the properties of their constituent elements, including aggregation, generalization, and instantiation operations. The theoretical framework proposed includes a set of expansion-based algorithms to execute these operations, and an application case is presented to illustrate the model's effectiveness.

This research investigates the impact of varying annealing time precision on the effectiveness and optimal settings of a specific category of classical Ising-type quantum annealers that employ semi-classical control techniques. Specifically, our studies focus on instances of the exact cover problem solved using two distinct approaches: static and sudden quenches. Our experimental setup involved running multiple instances of a carefully selected diagonal ratchet problem, both with accurate and imprecise parameter sets obtained through sudden quenches, which facilitated the identification of their appropriate influence on instance complexity. Furthermore, we conducted experiments with randomly generated instances that were comparable in size, utilizing both accurate and imprecise instances to demonstrate that our observations were also applicable to a broader range of instances. Our findings showed that the number of operations necessary to achieve a certain level of accuracy grew at a slower rate than previously thought when the annealing time was changed with high precision. In addition, we found that the optimal settings for the transverse field and interaction strength varied significantly in a nonlinear and non-monotonic manner.

Infinite-layer nickelate NiO shows a lot of similarities to cuprates and has a high
potential for achieving superconductivity. Theoretical calculations reveal that
Ni atoms in the conduction bands have three distinct states with different levels
of symmetry. We investigate the impact of strong screening effects in a model
that accounts for two conduction bands. Our findings suggest that when the
screening effect is pronounced, a bound state forms between the two bands and
results in a stable, filled 3d9 configuration associated with an infinite-life
resonance. As temperature increases, this bound state breaks apart into three
separate phases that correspond to high, middle, and low energy holes found
on the Ni atoms. Unexpectedly, despite having the same amount of doping, the
middle energy holes exhibit different characteristics than the high and low
energy holes. The three phases display different behaviors with respect to
middle-hole-to-low-hole transfer and the two phases show distinct features in
their effective potential.

The dense stellar matter that makes up neutron stars could consist of neutrons, electrons, and quarks, and we investigate the sound speed in quark matter using the Nambu-Jona-Lashio model, taking into account its fermion nature. The equation of state for dense quark matter is a combination of a relativistic gas and an anharmonic oscillator, and we express the speed of sound in quark matter as a function of baryon density, assuming both non-interacting and interactor quark matter. The presence of a critical density where sound ceases to propagate is identified, and we determine the speed of sound in dense stellar matter by incorporating the anharmonic gas model into the relativistic star structure equations. The resulting outcomes are visualized in density-s-radius diagrams for both neutral and charged matter within neutron stars.

This research involves a mathematical concept known as a "compass system," which is used to explore the properties of a space called a Fock space. The study focuses on the effects of two operations, compression and shift, on the structure and relationships within this space. The compass system provides a framework for understanding how these operations interact with one another, forming a form of symmetry. The research demonstrates that a shift in origin does not alter the fundamental nature of a signal while compression affects its temporal scale. The mathematical concepts of a shift and a dilation are shown to be compatible with one another, allowing the expression of a "distance" between points in the space. The discussion extends to the application of this idea in music theory.

The formation of planets in the outer areas of protoplanetary disks faces a challenge caused by dust, which can create an instability known as vertical shear instability (VSI). This VSI, capable of scavenging gas within the disk, is influenced by the behavior of dust, yet it is not clearly understood. As a result, we created a series of three-dimensional simulations to better grasp how the VSI interacts with dust and how this in turn impacts the distribution of dust in the disk and available fuel for planet formation. It becomes apparent that the VSI and dust heavily influence each other, leading to a pattern where dusty regions give rise to more intense VSI, which in turn results in less dust by enhancing gas mixing. In addition, we found that environments with high aspect ratios favor rapid planet formation by the growth of solid particles, especially in scenarios with lower levels of turbulence. As a result, large planets could form within a few thousand years, whereas smaller ones would emerge within ten thousand years as described by a power law in relation to the vertical scale of the instability.

This research paper establishes an improved Liouville theorem for submanifolds within a specific type of space, those with limited and constant scalar curvature. Our innovation builds upon the work of Biquard and Linear, who proved that a submanifold with a constant positive curvature must be spherical. We extend this result to show that any complete submanifold with constant scalar curvature in these spaces must be flat. Additionally, we determine that any complete submanifold in a space of negative constant curvature must also have negative or flat curvature. These findings provide valuable insights into the geometric properties of submanifolds in spaces with limited or constant scalar curvature.

This work presents a new approach to addressing the task of video entry detection in urban surveillance footage. The primary objective of this project is to adapt an existing model, originally designed for transaction detection, and successfully transfer it to a more visually diverse domain. The domain shift poses significant challenges due to its inter-class diversity and low sample count. To effectively manage this difficulty, we propose two primary solutions. The first involves a novel training strategy, dynamic input selection, which aims to simplify the classification task by filtering out visually diverse data. The second approach, global pooling, seeks to mimic the complexity of urban scenes' visual diversity. The proposed methods demonstrate substantial performance improvements compared to baseline models, achieving precise detection of diverse and previously unseen events across multiple datasets.

In our research, we analyzed general relativity using alternative theories of gravity in accordance with the Parametrized Post-Newtonian framework. We identified and reformed errors in the equations of motion for solar system objects, specifically related to the $v^3$ acceleration term, which may influence observational data similar to that produced by the Gaia mission. We calculated the resulting effects on observational data for Earth and Mars, discovering a possible systematic error of up to 0.76 mas for parallax measurements. We created a method to mitigate this uncertainty and applied it to a simulation of solar system object movements. Our results indicate that integrating known PPN parameters, particularly those affecting the solar mass, could lead to more accurate astrometric observations, potentially reducing uncertainty in Gaia-like measurements by approximately an order of magnitude.

Open-domain commonsense question-answering (QC) demands careful knowledge reasoning to produce answers that are semantically linked and consider the nuances of language, in contrast to mere technically correct responses on exam-style questions. In the careful semantic insight responding task, the ideal answer should be accurate, coherent, relevant, and refined, reflecting a response of high-quality reasoning and language. To achieve this, we introduced the Careful Semantic Insight Question Dataset (CSIQ), consisting of 600 carefully constructed questions and answers centered around everyday objects, animals, and people. Each question-answer pair is designed to be responsive to an initial draft, aiming to reflect a response that has been refined for perfection. To evaluate the difficult semantic reasoning required in these questions, we suggest the Concept-Link Reasoning Length (C-LRL) metric, which we believe correlates with the complexity of the reasoning needed to answer the questions. Our analysis reveals a strong correlation (0.73) between C-LRL and another reasoning length indicator, thus validating our proposed metric's effectiveness. To address the CSIQ's challenging nature, we conducted a comparative study of three baselines and two sophisticated models that leverage visual concepts and careful reinforcement learning. Our findings demonstrate that exploiting visual concepts and incorporating directional feedback through careful reinforcement learning enhances the ability to respond to these complex questions. Furthermore, we believe the CSIQ and our analysis are valuable resources for advancing research in vQA and QC models that aim to respond to open-domain questions with considered

Asteroidal and cometal substances contain a vast array of compounds with oxygen in various forms, including highly unstable molecular cations that may play a crucial role in interstellar chemical reactions, although this assumption is currently not well-supported. Despite being found through both laboratory experiments and observations, many of these molecular cations, such as H2O+, CO+, and CO2+, have ambiguous or inconsistent frequency data, hindering the effective analysis of electrical discharges in cometary environments. Such discrepancies hinder accurate comparisons between observed spectra and research findings, potentially masking important insights in the study of comets. As a result, current research on the electrical discharges in comets is hampered, limiting a comprehensive understanding of the actual composition of these celestial bodies. To rectify this challenge, there is an imperative need for enhanced research efforts aimed at developing more reliable data interpretation methods in the context of cometary spectroscopy.

In the context of horizontal federated learning, variations in data distributions across clients pose a substantial obstacle, rendering standard algorithms ineffective and slowing down model training. Standard approaches to overcome this challenge require either the aggregation of model updates by a central server, which contradicts the primary purpose of FL, or the assumption of identical data distributions among clients, which is often unrealistic. We introduce "Stroll for Education," a straightforward and effective strategy that enables clients to select non-i.i.d. update samples based on a random "walk," thereby providing an improved model. Our approach not only results in a more accurate model but also is easily implementable, has minimal memory requirements, does not necessitate the coordination of a central server, and is applicable in the context of FL. Our results show that our approach outperforms existing methods in various experiments, including those involving a prolonged training process with varying data distributions across clients.

The effects of mandatory counseling and therapy within the criminal justice system on mental health are being scrutinized, with limitations of current research highlighted and the proposed perspective discussing potential detrimental impacts of such requirements. These effects include anxiety resulting from unavoidable counseling sessions, damage to self-esteem caused by forced counseling, increased compliance through shame and self-interest, and strategies to minimize harm through optional volunteer counseling, gradual implementation, and providing valuable information to participants. Furthermore, this document contrasts voluntary and mandatory counseling and lists various approaches used in the criminal justice system for counseling.

Medical image analysis is a vast and intricate field with numerous applications, including examination, treatment planning, and surgery. It often involves examining images such as MRI, CT, and ultrasound to visualize internal body structures. One key challenge in this field is accurately and efficiently segmenting these images into distinct parts. Although recent techniques have made significant improvements, they rely on fully annotated data, which is time-consuming and expensive to obtain. This paper introduces a new, unique technique that uses semi-supervised learning to achieve better results with only a small amount of labeled data. This technique employs a consistent technique for generating additional data by using a technique called data augmentation. This approach is distinct from previous methods that employed different types of annotations for training. The proposed technique has been tested and compared to the latest state-of-the-art techniques using five different examination sets including the 3D SCA, the ACDC, the Me3D-SCT, the Me3D-LA, and the Me3D-AMC collections. This technique outperforms recent methods and demonstrates significant improvements in various assessments including the DSC, the 95% HD, and the volume errors in all examinations included in the experiments.

Lewis structure theory provides the basis for predicting a dynamical system's stability by examining its orbit's stability under initial condition changes, yet this approach is limited to linear systems due to its inherent linearity. This research reinterprers $\Lambda$ as the first Lyapunov exponent and leverages the Gross-Pitaevskii equation to examine the dynamics of a single trapped Bose-Einstein condensate within a 1D periodic box. The study employs the chaotic dynamics of a single atom to predict first the Lyapunov spectrum of the system and then explores the influence of the mean field on chaotic behavior. To effectively track single-atom dynamics within the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, this research develops a custom graph neural network, capable of accurately predicting future states and identifying the complexity of initial conditions. The research establishes an inverse relationship between the first Lyapunov exponent and $\gamma$ (gamma), representing the degree of chaos, which is observable even at low pitanevski regimes.

Let $\ell(p_1,\ldots, p_n | y)$ be a likelihood function for the parameter of interest $\bar{p}$, given data $y$. We define a generalized maximum likelihood estimator $\widehat{\bar{p}}_{GML}$ as the value that maximizes the likelihood function $\ell(\cdot | y)$. We prove that if a certain condition holds, then the generalized maximum likelihood estimator of $\bar{p}$, given by $\argmax_{\bar{p}} \sum_{j=1}^n \omega_j \log \left\{ \sum_{k=1}^K \exp \left\{ a_k(\bar{p}) + b_k(\bar{p}) \right\} \right\}$, where $\sum_j \omega_j = 1$, equals the weighted average of the standard maximum likelihood estimators of $p_j$. Deep learning knowledge tracing has seen rapid development lately. State-of-the-art models like DKN, ATMaster, and F-AT have outperformed traditional methods. To facilitate the evaluation of deep learning knowledge tracing models, we created pyKT, a Python framework providing ready-to-use datasets and modules for model development and assessment. We included 4 popular deep learning knowledge tracing models in the framework and gathered 5 standard datasets for testing. The framework has garnered positive feedback from users and the research community, with 49 GitHub stars and 4 issues within the first month. We received 4 submissions for the Educational Data Mining Society's code track at the 9th EDM conference in 2021, 3 of which were based on the pyKT framework. We documented the framework with examples and an atlas to guide users. pyKT streamlines deep learning knowledge tracing model evaluation and encourages collaboration and comparison among researchers.

The proof of a specific statement regarding differential operators is presented, which implies that for any differentiable function, the image of this operator encompasses the right-hand side of an arbitrary elliptic differential operator with varying coefficients, within the context of differentiable manifolds and employs Sobolev spaces. Additionally, this statement is applicable in the differentiation exact sequence. Moreover, several other consequences are discussed, including a difference between the image of differential operators on closed sub-manifolds and on differentiable varieties, where in the latter case, the image is not even closed, as well as a distinction in the differential cohomology of closed sub-manifolds and on differentiable varieties.

The recent launch of Alethe, a new format for representing resolved proofs using SMT solvers, is described in this format which aims, along with other benefits, to provide a unified basis for results produced by SMT solvers and linked libraries that generate proofs. This is illustrated by the ability to import Coq and Gaia proofs, as well as through the ease of manipulating these proofs with the PaV development environment and the proof checker PaV.

We examine the synchronous buffered aggregation (SBA) setting for distributed model training.
In this setting, a central server gathers randomly selected model updates from multiple clients to revise the current model, which is then shared with the next group of models.
This method has been widely adopted in various applications like distributed model training in AI.
However, we discovered that during each iteration, the current model may not be optimal for all models since some models have already been trained with an outdated version of the model.
To take advantage of this, we introduce two techniques that modify the traditional distributed training process.
The first technique, known as model shift compensation (MSC), uses the difference in model difficulty to adjust model updates.
Alternatively, we propose a tuned difficulty index to approximate updated models' difficulty in the second technique.
Neither of these methods requires any additional computational effort or changes to the current design of distributed systems.
As a result, we can successfully enhance the performance of a large number of models with varying difficulties with negligible cost.
Our method successfully demonstrates that SBA can lead to an improved performance of models by varying degrees of difficulty.

An interesting bideirectional transfer ability of automatic speech recognition
models has been recently found, even though it was not originally intended. It has
been shown that training an ASR model on a simple dataset containing only a few
distinct words can significantly enhance its performance in translating the
transcriptions produced by a high-quality model for texts that are either complex or
across different languages. Furthermore, it has been found that the reverse
transfer is also feasible, as pre-training on a real text allows an ASR model to
outperform a another ASR model on a synthetic dataset in a cross-language
scenario. Using a simple but highly effective transfer framework, a model that is
based on a neural transducer has been trained to decode rough transcriptions in a
way that mirrors a model that is trained on a high-quality corpus, allowing for
accurate decoding of a wide range of texts, including those that are complex or
across different languages.

Autonomous systems are increasingly deployed for ocean research, but they are limited by the need for human operation. To navigate effectively, they must N-way classify paths to avoid collisions. Traditional methods for this classification rely on real-time processing of sensor data. In contrast, our approach focuses on estimating the underlying distribution of path classifications to reduce classification complexity. By modeling path class probabilities as a Gaussian Process that depends on time, we can capture the data's temporal dynamics and extrapolate beyond observed time periods. This allows the system to anticipate paths with higher variance and prioritize them for sampling, enabling more efficient data collection. Our approach is demonstrated using data from an autonomous surface vehicle in the ocean, showing the system's ability to classify paths and guide the robot accordingly.

We provide explicit manifestations of non-uniform "celestial" fluid configurations within the framework of General Relativity, which feature a flat cylindrical wavefront enveloping constant-density interior spheres, both filled with fluid substances that adhere to the equation of state $p=\sigma \rho$. By leveraging the Theorem by Blume, these configurations are demonstrated to be solutions for a broad spectrum of dimensions ($D\geq 4$), dimensions in which a uniform two-fluid sphere was previously shown to be impossible. It was previously established that uniform two-fluid spheres are feasible only in higher dimensions ($D\geq 9$), and we show that distinct scenarios can be customized to meet the requirements of specific dimensions, illustrating that $D=5$ can be achieved with the $\sigma =0.48$ value.

Most current methods for correcting grammatical errors rely on data from the same domain, which leads to poor performance when applied to data from a different domain. This performance decline is particularly severe when there's very little data available in the new domain. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach that uses a small amount of data from the target domain to transfer knowledge from a source domain. The proposed method employs a meta-learning strategy to transfer knowledge from the source domain. This approach enables a model trained on a source domain to quickly adapt and perform well on a new domain with minimal data. The proposed model achieves state-of-the-art results on two popular datasets, and it surpasses strong baseline approaches in terms of performance.

For resource allocation problems where resources are not divisible, we examine situations where all agents are fully informed about the valuation functions associated with the resources and act in a strategic manner. We focus on two standard allocation mechanisms - First-Come-First-Served (FCFS) and Highest-Bid-Wins (HBW) - and establish existence proofs for pure Nash equilibria for a wide variety of valuation functions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that any pure Nash equilibrium achieved through these mechanisms satisfies the equitable solution principle, showing that all agents either obtain nothing or are deployed in identical quantities with the same valuations. We also show that these mechanisms admit at least one efficient pure Nash equilibrium, which can be proven to be a global maximum.

This paper presents an unusually clear visualization of a galaxy's disk structure, achieved by using a one-week-long one-dimensional light curve from the Kepler space telescope of the galaxy UGC 8839. By applying the Fourier transform method to its light pattern, the structural features of the galaxy were analyzed. Spectroscopic observations, conducted with the VLT/MUSE instrument, confirmed that the periodic signals originate from an extremely stable spiral arm structure rather than from variable stars. It is hypothesized that this formation is artificial, likely resulting from past interactions between UGC 8839 and nearby galaxies, with evidence of past galaxy encounters supporting this theory. The research also highlights the potential for using high-precision external variables, such as spiral arms, for creating more accurate distance measurements in galaxies.

This study combines two-cURRENT relations to integrate experimental data into a precise examination of the pion's structure. A re-evaluation of hadron models shows that the coupling between a pion and a pair of photons offers a sensitive method for probing the balance between its point-like and constituent components. Through the two-current framework, multiple relations linking the scalar, vector, and tensor charges are established. A new calculation of the scalar charge $\sigma_\pi$ is undertaken, along with assessments of vector charge and tensor charge which form dimensions of key hadron tensors. These efforts facilitate a direct comparison between various models and both experimental data and future lattice calculations.

A survey conducted over three years using the PdI X-ray telescope on twelve known optical/infrared sources with previously unconfirmed magnetic accretion mechanisms revealed both reversible and non-reversible switchings of the X-ray emission of several objects, including a notable case with the object XX Cha exhibiting unique, wide amplitude fluctuations in its accretion rates. Based on extensive monitoring and analysis, the exchange rates of ionized hydrogen for XX Cha are estimated, showing an unusually broad range that far exceeds what was previously known. This particular object's behavior is attributed to its short orbital period, which results in the interaction between its binary components and ultimately influences its high accretion rates.

In offline multi-agent settings, an agent is required to navigate the environment alongside other agents, with the goal of reaching a positive outcome while avoiding dangerous situations. To achieve this, offline learning methods utilize carefully selected episodes where the other agents have led to desirable results. However, existing offline algorithms focus primarily on single-agent learning, neglecting the interdependencies of learning from other agents' experiences. This paper investigates offline multi-agent learning from positive trajectories with an emphasis on cooperative settings, presenting two novel approaches that leverage the structure of multi-agent interactions to enhance the performance of a single agent. A comparative analysis is presented with state-of-the-art single-agent offline methods, demonstrating that mutual information estimation yields promising results under certain conditions, while mutual relevance decomposition outperforms other basics under different scenarios.

We investigated the use of 2D or volumetric MV images as input for a convolutional neural network to enhance their alignment with CT images.  Our goal was to establish a consistent modality type that yields the best results in terms of task performance.  Our evaluation involved using both flat-field and log-scaled MV images as references.  The proposed method was successfully applied to both 2D and volumetric MV images.  In comparison to using feature-based methods, our approach demonstrated significant improvements in accuracy, particularly with volumetric data.  Furthermore, we observed that the optimal results were achieved when flat-field MV images were used as input, particularly with 2D data.

Single-particle Fock states, when guided by a local non-classical amplitude, have long been regarded as a single-particle form of entanglement. It has also been suggested that such entangled states are necessary and sufficient for exhibiting nonlocal guidance effects in interaction-based measurements. To further explore this, we theoretically investigate the guidance effect arising from a single-photon entangled state in an actual experiment, utilizing a high-speed, low-sensitivity detector that doesn't require particle interaction. We find that local guidance indeed constrains the achievable rate of a nonlocal Bell-type test, but surprisingly, it's not sufficient to maximize the Bell inequality's violation. This is in contrast to previous theories, which predicted single-particle entanglement to be sufficient for maximizing nonlocal guidance effects.

Advanced vehicular applications are increasingly dependent on shared V2V (Vehicular to Vehicular) learning systems. Yet, several issues obstruct the reliability and security of these collaborative approaches. A novel federated learning framework has been proposed to mitigate these problems by integrating various cutting-edge technologies, including (improved) Raft protocol, Federated Learning, and Blockchain. This paper examines various FV (Federated Vehicular) learning systems across a spectrum of applications, such as autonomous driving, V2V (autonomous and non-autonomous), and IVS (Intelligent Transportation Systems). This examination focuses on various aspects, such as the application of Federated Learning, an in-depth analysis of the proposed frameworks, and their respective advantages and disadvantages. This examination differs from other research that has conducted a simple topic survey. This examination differs from other research that has conducted a simpler topic survey. This examination differs from other research integrating various state-of-the-art technologies, such as FedLearn, by proposing novel federated frameworks. V392 Persei is the most recent explosive event involving the binary star V4641 Persei.
It was identified as a classic nova in 2018, but in May 2020, it exhibited
extraordinary signs of a hypernova, being both the most luminous in the gamma-ray
spectrum among nova stars a day prior to peak brightness and the most luminous in
the gamma-ray spectrum when approaching the peak of a nova star at any given
visual brightness level.
An examination of the gamma-ray data reveals that V392 Persei, at a day prior to
peak brightness, was among the group of novae displaying a high level of gamma-ray
brightness.
However, an analysis of optical and X-ray characteristics shows that on the day it
was observed, V392 Persei should have been classified as a typical, low-luminosity
nova star, which is on the smaller end of the spectrum of nova stars.
This exploration breaks down the gamma-ray properties of novae into subsets based
on their visual brightness levels and gamma-ray spectrum characteristics.
It compares the gamma-ray behavior of V392 Persei with other known events and
analyzes the physical mechanisms of gamma-ray generation in novae.
It also compares V392 Persei with other events of the same star and with
recurring gamma-ray novae.

A multiple-input multiple-output communication technique has been enhanced by addressing three key challenges. Initially, a Gaussian mixture model was shown to effectively model MIMO channel capacity and coherence, providing a theoretical foundation for codebook design. Building on this, an efficient algorithm was devised to create custom codebooks tailored to specific application requirements. Furthermore, an optimized feedback encoding method has been developed to maximize codebook utility by accurately reflecting changing channel conditions over time. These innovations are set in the context of an adaptive codebook in a frequency division duplexing system, but the underlying solutions are also applicable to other channel variation scenarios and communication architecture types.

We perform comprehensive, detailed calculations in a rigorous three-dimensional version of the Hofstadter model, which spans two spatial dimensions and experiences a constant, perpendicular magnetic field, as well as a constant, perpendicular electric field. Under these conditions, we discover robust surface current patterns that are topologically protected and reside on the material's surface in accordance with a three-dimensional analog of the bulk-edge correspondence principle. These surface currents are unaffected by imbalances in particle numbers.

Recent observations by the Voyager space probes were utilized to establish stricter limits on various physical processes taking place near the space probes, which were found to be moving through the interstellar medium. These processes, which could potentially cause significant energy losses for stellar objects, were found to result in a maximum mass accretion rate of 10 times 10^-6. The new data from the Voyager space probes are expected to lead to improved constraints on such processes, which could lead to more accurate estimates of the maximum mass accretion rate of 10^-5.

The initial stars that populated galaxies likely formed within star clusters at the centers of galaxies, and many of these stars were massive and compact, situated in environments with high stellar densities known as star clusters. Over time, these stars interacted with their surroundings, eventually merging and contributing to the formation of the most massive objects in the universe. The remnants of these high-density stellar environments remain underexplored using current detection methods for cosmic events. By applying detailed simulations of these clusters, this research predicts that the remnants of these initial stars will produce detectable gravitational signals, revealing new insights into the nature of matter and space-time, and providing a framework for understanding the universe's complex history.

An auxiliary layer protection mechanism is introduced in this study to enhance the security of Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) based wireless communications with Amplify and Forward (AF) relays. By constraining the transmission rates of direct communication links and utilizing additional transmit power, interference is directed towards the reception points of compromised nodes during time periods when relays are inactive. A new problem formulation is then developed to maximize the sum transmission rate while safeguarding against eavesdropping and staying within power limits. Due to the non-convex nature of this problem, a method is proposed to find a near-optimal feasible solution by drawing on existing results. Furthermore, two specialized scenarios are analyzed and solved efficiently. Both theoretical and simulation data confirm the enhanced security and throughput provided by this physical layer protection mechanism.

Text-based adventure games present a simple world model with rich interactive possibilities, high reward execution speed, and a need for effective language processing. These features make them suitable for developing strong artificial intelligence agents. Our analysis reveals that the simplest text-based adventure game genre, ExpressWorld, can be navigated at a high frequency, producing one million moves per second. Our world agent achieves exceptional performance on this platform, surpassing the previous record by four orders of magnitude, and breaking the one-second mark for solving complex text-based adventure games. Our research includes advancements in language policy, language model fine-tuning, and high-frequency world interaction.

Our research presents a novel energy-efficient approach for accurate video id, comprising both an optimized LSTM algorithm and an associated hardware implementation. In the algorithm development, we address three key aspects: a compact input representation method to reduce processing load, an iterative strategy to effectively utilize the memory capacity of LSTM, and an energy-efficient alternative to traditional activation functions. Our experiments demonstrate an average processing speed increase of 4.7 times, along with a 60% reduction in memory usage and the elimination of bottlenecks associated with activation functions. Building upon this efficient algorithm, we designed an adaptable and modular LSTM hardware architecture featuring three primary components: a memory access controller (MAC32), a MAC32-optimized MAC (OMAC32), and a MAC32-based MAC (SMAC32). Our research shows that this architecture can achieve a throughputs of 21.28 GFLOPS, 42.56 GFLOPS, and 85.12 GFLOPS respectively, with energy efficiencies of 0.98 GFLOPS/W, 1.96 GFLOPS/W, and 3.92 GFLOPS/W. Our optimized hardware architecture is capable of processing an entire video in under 40 minutes.

Given a Noetherian local ring, we can define the compact Hilbert polynomial and expansion as extensions to ideals, and we've identified multiple properties that indicate the $I$-F- purity or $I$- $F$- splitness of a ring in relation to these definitions, with results that hold under certain conditions over fields of positive characteristic.
